method: The paper provides a perspective on why constants matter, drawing analogies to Fisher information and Pinsker's constant, and illustrates with large-alphabet uniformity testing and calibration testing.
result: Sharp constants distinguish between rate-optimal tests, reveal effective signal-to-noise ratios, and guide tuning-parameter choices.
conclusion: Constants are crucial for practical distribution testing, and the same logic applies to calibration testing.

title: Controllability And Exponential Mixing In Singular Interacting Particle Systems
authors: Laurent Mertz, Vahagn Nersesyan, Manuel Rissel
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article concerns interacting particle systems with singular kernels, driven either by degenerate deterministic controls or by degenerate decomposable noise. In the deterministic setting, we establish global exact controllability and a topologically robust property called solid controllability. Moreover, we prove a result that guarantees global approximate controllability with prescribed trajectories. For stochastic dynamics, we obtain ergodicity and exponential mixing by utilizing coupling and recurrence mechanisms based on controllability. Our approach exploits the singularity and applies to a broad class of models, including Biot-Savart, Coulomb, Riesz, and Yukawa interactions, as well as heterogeneous multi-species systems.
tldr: This paper studies controllability and exponential mixing in interacting particle systems with singular kernels, using deterministic and stochastic control.
motivation: To understand controllability and ergodic properties of singular interacting particle systems, which are important in fluid dynamics and plasma physics.
method: The authors prove global exact controllability and solid controllability for deterministic systems, and establish ergodicity and exponential mixing for stochastic systems using coupling and recurrence mechanisms based on controllability.
result: They obtain global exact controllability, solid controllability, and global approximate controllability with prescribed trajectories for deterministic dynamics, and ergodicity with exponential mixing for stochastic dynamics.
conclusion: The singularity of interactions is exploited to achieve strong controllability and mixing properties, applicable to a broad class of models including Biot-Savart, Coulomb, Riesz, and Yukawa interactions.

title: Learning Ldpc Codes With Quantized Density Evolution Over Relaxed Protographs
authors: Gennady Shutkov, Dmitry Artemasov, Alexey Frolov, Pavel Rybin, Kirill Andreev
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the design of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes for a given iterative decoder. Despite tools such as direct simulation, density evolution (DE), and EXIT-chart analysis, selecting a parity-check matrix remains a difficult combinatorial optimization problem. Existing approaches often rely on population-based search, random mutations, genetic algorithms, or related heuristics, which require careful parameter tuning and may be computationally expensive. Recent gradient descent (GD)-based methods optimize relaxed parity-check matrices by differentiating through decoder simulations. However, such decoder-in-the-loop strategies rely on noisy Monte Carlo estimates, require line search over soft matrix representations, and remain costly for long LDPC codes. Moreover, although optimization is performed in a relaxed domain, the loss is typically evaluated only at integer-valued parity-check matrices. In this work, we focus on the design of long protograph-based LDPC codes and propose a deterministic GD-based framework that operates directly on a relaxed protograph representation. Each protograph entry is interpreted as the probability that the corresponding element is equal to one. The loss function is based on DE bit error rate (BER) performance and can be evaluated directly for relaxed protographs. To justify this relaxation, we associate the relaxed representation with an ensemble of binary protographs and show that the proposed relaxed DE gives the ensemble-averaged DE performance. The resulting optimization procedure is fully autonomous and uses standard GD methods. Owing to deterministic DE evaluation and informative gradients, the proposed approach provides fast and reliable convergence. Numerical experiments for the min-sum decoder show that the optimized protographs outperform 5G LDPC codes with the same protograph dimensions.
tldr: This paper proposes a gradient-descent-based method for designing LDPC codes using relaxed protographs and quantized density evolution.
motivation: Designing LDPC codes for iterative decoders is a combinatorial optimization problem; existing heuristic methods are computationally expensive and require careful tuning.
method: The authors interpret each protograph entry as a probability and use a deterministic gradient descent framework with a loss function based on density evolution bit error rate, evaluated directly on relaxed protographs.
result: The optimized protographs outperform 5G LDPC codes with the same protograph dimensions for the min-sum decoder.
conclusion: The proposed method provides fast and reliable convergence for designing long protograph-based LDPC codes without noisy Monte Carlo estimates.

title: Limits Of Uniform Certification In The Standard Turing Model -- Semantic Invariants And Admissible Methods
authors: Fabio F. G. Buono
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper does not address the mathematical truth of P versus NP. Instead, it identifies a structural limitation of uniform proof-generation methods in the standard Turing model. The observation is model-theoretic: it concerns the interaction between semantic invariants and syntactic verification, not the provability of complexity statements. We formalise an admissible method as a generator-verifier pair that produces, for each program, a finite certificate establishing a semantic property. Admissibility forces the generator-verifier composition to behave uniformly with respect to the invariant being certified. In the standard model, such uniform semantic certification implicitly induces a decision procedure for the property. Rice's theorem shows that this implicit behaviour cannot be realised for non-trivial semantic invariants, revealing a structural constraint on formal certification. Understanding this requires a meta-computational perspective: the obstruction arises from the computational behaviour induced by certification, not from the complexity-theoretic status of the property. We apply this framework to two semantic invariants naturally associated with formal certification of P vs. NP and with cryptographic hardness assumptions (in particular, one-way functions). Both fall under the same limitation: no uniform admissible method can certify them in the standard model. A complete Coq formalisation is provided, capturing the extensional structure of admissible methods and the semantic-syntactic interaction underlying the result.
tldr: This paper identifies a structural limitation of uniform proof-generation methods in the standard Turing model using model-theoretic arguments and a Coq formalization.
motivation: The paper aims to show that certain semantic properties, including those related to P vs NP and cryptographic hardness, cannot be certified by uniform admissible methods in the standard Turing model.
method: The author formalizes admissible methods as generator-verifier pairs and uses Rice's theorem to demonstrate that uniform semantic certification implicitly induces a decision procedure, which is impossible for non-trivial semantic invariants.
result: The paper proves that no uniform admissible method can certify the semantic invariants associated with P vs NP or one-way functions in the standard Turing model.
conclusion: The limitation is structural and model-theoretic, not complexity-theoretic, and applies to formal certification of certain semantic properties.

title: Degree-Constrained Interval Optimization For Minimax Polynomial Approximation In Homomorphic Encryption
authors: Jiheon Woo, Donggyun Ryu, Yongjune Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Homomorphic encryption (HE) enables privacy-preserving inference under arithmetic constraints that restrict encrypted evaluation to additions and multiplications. As a result, non-polynomial activation functions must be replaced by polynomial approximations. Among polynomial approximation methods, minimax approximation, typically computed by the Remez algorithm, is a standard approach because it minimizes the maximum approximation error over a given design interval. For minimax polynomial design, the approximation interval is a critical hyperparameter: a wider interval improves robustness to large-magnitude inputs while increasing the minimax approximation error under a fixed degree budget. In this paper, we formulate this trade-off as a distribution-aware interval optimization problem, where the approximation interval is chosen to minimize the mean-squared error (MSE) with respect to the pre-activation distribution of interest. To effectively control outside-interval inputs, we combine minimax polynomials with domain extension functions (DEFs) and their HE-realizable polynomial counterparts, domain extension polynomials (DEPs), which approximate a clipping operation outside the design interval and thereby suppress uncontrolled polynomial extrapolation. We first derive an analytically tractable DEF-based proxy objective that captures the trade-off between within-interval minimax approximation error and outside-interval clipping error. We then connect this idealized objective to HE-realizable DEP constructions through an implementation-error decomposition with an accompanying upper bound.
tldr: This paper proposes a degree-constrained interval optimization method for minimax polynomial approximation in homomorphic encryption, focusing on privacy-preserving inference.
motivation: Homomorphic encryption requires polynomial approximations of non-polynomial functions, and the choice of approximation interval critically affects accuracy and robustness.
method: The authors formulate a distribution-aware interval optimization problem to minimize mean-squared error, and combine minimax polynomials with domain extension functions to control outside-interval inputs.
result: They derive an analytically tractable proxy objective and connect it to HE-realizable polynomial constructions via an implementation-error decomposition.
conclusion: The proposed method improves the trade-off between approximation error and input robustness for polynomial approximations in HE.

title: Locality Of Curve-Decoding And Improved Proximity Gaps
authors: Rohan Goyal, Venkatesan Guruswami, Yihang Sun, Mary Wootters
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08516v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proximity gaps are a property of error correcting codes that arise in the study of Interactive Oracle Proofs (IOPs) and Succinct Non-interactive Arguments of Zero Knowledge (SNARKs). Recent work of Goyal and Guruswami has established near-optimal proximity gaps for many families of codes, including subspace design codes, as well as random ensembles like random linear codes, Reed-Solomon codes with random evaluation points, and Gallager's ensemble of LDPC codes (Goyal & Guruswami, 2025). However, the parameters for these latter randomized ensembles are worse than the parameters for subspace design codes, and degrade as the degree ell increases. In this work, we obtain improved proximity gaps for random ensembles of codes, including random linear codes, Reed-Solomon codes with random evaluation points, and Gallager's ensemble. Quantitatively, our results for these random ensembles match the results that Goyal and Guruswami attained for subspace design codes. In fact, our techniques are a black-box transference from subspace design codes: any progress on subspace design codes will automatically lead to analogous progress for these random ensembles. To obtain our results, we extend the Local Coordinate-wise Linear (LCL) property framework developed by Levi, Mosheiff, and Shagrithaya and by Brakensiek, Chen, Dhar, and Zhang to a version (Levi, Mosheiff & Shagrithaya, 2025; Brakensiek, Chen, Dhar & Zhang, 2025). This allows us to cast -- a property that implies proximity gaps -- directly as a row-span constrained LCL property, and make use of that machinery. In contrast, because curve-decodability is not obviously a vanilla LCL property, prior work had worked with a proxy property instead, leading to the aforementioned parameter losses.
tldr: This paper improves proximity gaps for random code ensembles by extending the LCL property framework to curve-decodability.
motivation: Proximity gaps are crucial for IOPs and SNARKs, but prior results for random codes had worse parameters than subspace design codes.
method: The authors extend the Local Coordinate-wise Linear (LCL) property framework to cast curve-decodability as a row-span constrained LCL property, enabling a black-box transfer from subspace design codes.
result: They achieve proximity gaps for random linear codes, Reed-Solomon codes, and Gallager's LDPC codes that match the best known parameters for subspace design codes.
conclusion: The work provides a general technique to transfer proximity gap results from subspace design codes to random code ensembles, improving their applicability in cryptographic proofs.

title: On The Convergence Of Belief Propagation For Multipath Data Association In Target Tracking
authors: Kuilong Yang, Zengfu Wang, Hua Lan, Jing Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Belief propagation (BP) is widely used for data association (DA) in target tracking. Existing convergence analyses of BP for DA address only the two-way correspondence between targets and measurements, where each target generates at most one measurement per scan. Multipath DA (MPDA) allows a single target to produce multiple measurements via distinct propagation paths, creating a three-way correspondence among targets, paths, and measurements, for which a complete convergence proof has not yet been provided. We provide such a proof for the BP updates in MPDA, establishing convergence to a unique fixed point. Simulations illustrate the convergence behavior of BP in MPDA and demonstrate a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off relative to both single-scan and two-scan variants of the multiple-detection multiple-hypothesis tracker.
tldr: This paper proves convergence of belief propagation for multipath data association in target tracking, a classical multi-target tracking problem.
motivation: Existing convergence analyses of BP for data association only cover two-way correspondence; multipath DA involves three-way correspondence and lacks a convergence proof.
method: The authors provide a convergence proof for BP updates in multipath DA by formulating the problem as a factor graph and showing the BP iterations converge to a unique fixed point.
result: Simulations demonstrate convergence behavior and a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off compared to multiple-detection multiple-hypothesis trackers.
conclusion: BP for multipath DA converges to a unique fixed point, enabling efficient and accurate tracking in scenarios with multiple detections per target.

title: Achieving Unanimous Consensus Through Multi-Agent Deliberation
authors: Apurba Pokharel, Ram Dantu, Shakila Zaman, Vinh Quach, Sirisha Talapuru
abstract: ArXiv:2504.02128v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Blockchain consensus mechanisms have relied on algorithms such as Proof-of-Work (PoW) and Proof-of-Stake (PoS) to ensure network functionality and integrity. However, these approaches struggle with adaptability for decision-making where the opinions of each matter rather than reaching an agreement based on honest majority or weighted consensus. This paper introduces a novel deliberation-based consensus mechanism where Large Language Models (LLMs) act as rational agents engaging in structured discussions to reach a unanimous consensus. By leveraging graded consensus and a multi-round deliberation process, our approach ensures unanimous consensus for definitive problems and graded consensus for prioritized decision problems and policies. We provide a formalization of our system and use it to show that the properties of blockchains are maintained, while also addressing the behavior in terms of adversaries, stalled deliberations, and confidence in consensus. Moreover, experimental results demonstrate system feasibility, showcasing convergence, block properties, and accuracy, which enable deliberative decision-making on blockchain networks.
tldr: This paper proposes a blockchain consensus mechanism using LLM agents to achieve unanimous or graded consensus through structured deliberation.
motivation: Traditional blockchain consensus mechanisms like PoW and PoS lack adaptability for opinion-based decision-making where each participant's view matters.
method: The authors design a multi-round deliberation process where LLM agents discuss and update their positions, using graded consensus to reach agreement.
result: Experimental results show feasibility, convergence, block properties, and accuracy, demonstrating deliberative decision-making on blockchain networks.
conclusion: The proposed deliberation-based consensus mechanism maintains blockchain properties while enabling more flexible consensus for decision-making problems.

title: Probing Individual Phonon-polaritonic Nanoparticle-on-mirror Cavities By Infrared Nanospectroscopy
authors: Isabel Pascual Robledo, Iker Herrero Le\'on, Karol Ko{\l}ataj, Guillermo P. Acuna, Javier Aizpurua, Philippe Roelli, Rainer Hillenbrand
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanoparticle-on-mirror (NPoM) cavities enable extreme light confinement and strong light-matter interactions, but their realization with phonon-polariton materials in the mid-infrared spectral range remains largely unexplored. Here, we use nano-FTIR spectroscopy to study the near-field response of individual phononic NPoM cavities formed by gold nanoparticles on a quartz substrate supporting phonon-polaritons. By placing a metal tip on top of the NPoM and recording the tip-scattered field, we observe two reproducible cavity resonances, identified as the fundamental and a second-order antenna modes by numerical simulations. The calculations show that, in absence of the tip, the NPoM cavity exhibits ultrasmall mode volumes ([MATH] nm[MATH]) and high quality factors ([MATH]), resulting in extraordinary field intensity enhancements ([MATH]) and Purcell factors ([MATH]). They also indicate that the nano-FTIR tip enables efficient excitation and readout of these phononic NPoM modes without perturbing them, while enhancing the intrinsic local field intensity in the NPoM gap by two orders of magnitude. Our results establish phononic NPoM cavities as a promising platform for mid-infrared nanophotonics and pave the way for ultrasensitive vibrational spectroscopy based on nano-FTIR measurements of individual cavities.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies phonon-polaritonic nanoparticle-on-mirror cavities in the mid-infrared using nano-FTIR spectroscopy, demonstrating extreme field confinement and high Purcell factors.
motivation: Nanoparticle-on-mirror cavities with phonon-polariton materials in the mid-infrared are largely unexplored, yet they promise strong light-matter interactions for nanophotonics and vibrational spectroscopy.
method: The authors use nano-FTIR spectroscopy with a metal tip to excite and read out cavity modes of gold nanoparticles on a quartz substrate, supported by numerical simulations.
result: Two cavity resonances are observed, identified as fundamental and second-order antenna modes. Simulations show ultrasmall mode volumes, high quality factors, and extraordinary field enhancements and Purcell factors.
conclusion: Phononic NPoM cavities are established as a promising platform for mid-infrared nanophotonics and ultrasensitive vibrational spectroscopy.

title: From Bayes' Rule To Bayes Rules: Optimal Information Processing And Axiomatic Foundations Beyond Probability
authors: Badr-Eddine Ch\'erief-Abdellatif Jeremie Houssineau
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops principled updating rules for possibilistic inference, where uncertainty about a fixed parameter is represented by a possibility function, the maxitive analogue of a probability distribution, and comparisons are made pointwise via a partial order. From two complementary foundations, an information-conservation viewpoint and an axiomatic viewpoint, we derive the same canonical update: the posterior is the prior-likelihood product followed by supremum normalisation. The two derivations agree for an arbitrary loss, differing only in where the learning-rate parameter enters. This parameter controls epistemic strength and is not identifiable from the normalising evidence alone, clarifying the role of analogous learning-rate parameters in generalised Bayesian updating.
tldr: This paper develops possibilistic inference updating rules based on information-conservation and axiomatic foundations, extending Bayesian reasoning to possibility functions.
motivation: To provide principled updating rules for possibilistic inference, where uncertainty is represented by possibility functions rather than probability distributions, and to clarify the role of learning-rate parameters in generalized Bayesian updating.
method: The authors derive a canonical update rule from two complementary foundations: an information-conservation viewpoint and an axiomatic viewpoint, both yielding the same posterior as the prior-likelihood product followed by supremum normalization.
result: The two derivations agree for an arbitrary loss, differing only in where the learning-rate parameter enters, which controls epistemic strength and is not identifiable from normalizing evidence alone.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for possibilistic inference and clarifies the role of learning-rate parameters in generalized Bayesian updating.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning-Empowered Wireless Sensor Networking For 6g Closed-Loop Controls
authors: Chengleyang Lei, Wei Feng, Yunfei Chen, Yongxu Zhu, Ning Ge, Shi Jin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robots are increasingly deployed in remote or hazardous areas for mission-critical control tasks. Due to their limited individual capabilities, they have to rely on other field sensors to obtain the state information of targets, and also a dedicated edge information hub (EIH) to enable information exchange, sensing data analysis and control command generation. Such configuration follows a sensing-communication-computing-control (SC3) closed loop. To optimize the whole closed-loop performance, this paper minimizes the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) control cost by designing the sensor-to-EIH bandwidth allocation. Specifically, we first model the distortion noise caused by limited communication data rate based on the mutual information theory. Next, under the control policy based on the Kalman filter and LQR controller, we formulate the control process as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), and develop a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based sensor-to-EIH bandwidth allocation scheme. The proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm is utilized to train the DRL agent. Simulation results are provided to show the superiority of the proposed DRL-based scheme.
tldr: This paper uses deep reinforcement learning to optimize bandwidth allocation in wireless sensor networks for 6G closed-loop control, minimizing LQR control cost.
motivation: Robots in remote/hazardous areas need efficient sensing-communication-computing-control loops; optimizing bandwidth allocation can improve control performance.
method: Models distortion noise via mutual information, formulates control as POMDP, and uses PPO algorithm to allocate sensor-to-EIH bandwidth.
result: Simulations show the DRL-based scheme outperforms baselines in reducing LQR control cost.
conclusion: DRL-based bandwidth allocation effectively enhances closed-loop control performance in wireless sensor networks.

title: Optimization And Deep Learning Based Resource Allocation For UAV-Aided Wireless Communication With Rotatable Antenna Array
authors: Fengcheng Pei, Lin Xiang, Anja Klein, Robert Schober
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-antenna unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-aided communication presents a promising solution to increase the system capacity and improve the quality of service (QoS) of the future wireless networks. In this paper, we equip a UAV platform with a rotatable antenna array (RAA), which can be rotated flexibly in three-dimensional (3D) space via an onboard gimbal, enabling additional spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) for improving multiuser signal transmission and interference management. Compared with a conventional fixed antenna array (FAA), the RAA can proactively align users with the high-gain region of its antenna elements and reduce the spatial channel correlations among users. To demonstrate the advantages of RAA, we jointly design the RAA orientation and beamforming to maximize the sum-rate of multiple users subject to per-user QoS constraints. The formulated problem is highly nonconvex and exhibits strong coupling between the RAA orientation and beamforming variables. To solve this challenging problem, we propose first an optimization framework based on the penalty dual decomposition (PDD) method to iteratively optimize RAA orientation and beamforming. While the optimization framework yields high reliability in QoS satisfaction and favorable sum-rate performance, its iterative nature may hinder real-time deployment. To accelerate the joint design and preserve a high-quality solution, we further propose a deep learning (DL) framework based on graph neural networks (GNNs). Simulation results demonstrate that RAAs significantly outperform FAAs in UAV-aided communication. Additionally, the proposed optimization framework is capable of satisfying stringent QoS requirements with high reliability, while the proposed DL framework attains comparable sum-rate performance with substantially reduced computation time and exhibits robustness to user position information errors.
tldr: This paper proposes optimization and deep learning methods for resource allocation in UAV-aided wireless communication with rotatable antenna arrays.
motivation: To improve system capacity and quality of service in future wireless networks by leveraging the additional spatial degrees of freedom from rotatable antenna arrays on UAVs.
method: Jointly designs RAA orientation and beamforming using a penalty dual decomposition optimization framework and a graph neural network-based deep learning framework.
result: RAAs significantly outperform fixed antenna arrays; the optimization framework satisfies stringent QoS requirements reliably, while the DL framework achieves comparable sum-rate with reduced computation time and robustness to errors.
conclusion: Rotatable antenna arrays combined with efficient optimization or deep learning can enhance UAV-aided wireless communication performance.

title: Neural And Spectral Operator Surrogates On Gaussian Spaces
authors: Carlo Marcati, Mario Mari\'c, Christoph Schwab, Jakob Zech
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove expression rate bounds of finite-parametric, spectral and neural surrogates for holomorphic maps between separable Hilbert spaces. The surrogates have an encoder-approximator-decoder architecture, with Karhunen-Lo\'{e}ve encoders and frame decoders. We prove expression rate bounds for two classes of finite-parametric surrogates: i) spectral surrogates obtained by N-term truncations of Wiener polynomial chaos expansions and ii) neural surrogates obtained by approximation of parametric maps with deep feedforward neural networks, ReLU and RePU activation functions and uniformly bounded weights. We work under an algebraic decay assumption on the eigenvalues of the covariance of the Gaussian measure on the input space. We obtain convergence rates for mean-square errors, and additionally in first-order Gaussian Sobolev spaces, to account for errors in the approximation of gradients.
tldr: This paper studies approximation rates of spectral and neural surrogates for holomorphic maps on Gaussian spaces, focusing on operator learning in infinite-dimensional settings.
motivation: To develop efficient surrogate models for parametric maps arising in uncertainty quantification and PDEs with random inputs.
method: Proves expression rate bounds for spectral surrogates (Wiener polynomial chaos) and neural surrogates (deep feedforward networks with ReLU/RePU) using Karhunen-Loève encoders and frame decoders under eigenvalue decay assumptions.
result: Obtains convergence rates for mean-square errors and first-order Gaussian Sobolev norms, showing algebraic rates depending on eigenvalue decay.
conclusion: Both spectral and neural surrogates achieve comparable approximation rates, with neural networks offering flexibility for high-dimensional problems.

title: Mlqenabler: Enabling Secure Machine Learning Queries Over Encrypted Database In Cloud Computing
authors: Xu Zhou, Haoyang Chen, Xinyu Lei
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In cloud computing, the public cloud service providers (CSPs) can provide cloud storage as the primary service while providing additional machine learning (ML)-based services by using the clients' data in storage. This business model extends the border of cloud computing services and brings in new business growth possibilities. Although it is promising, the model also brings in security concerns since the public commercial cloud cannot be fully trusted. For example, the public commercial clouds may sell clients' sensitive data to the government or other companies. To address the security concerns, an immediate solution is to require clients to encrypt their datasets before outsourcing to the cloud. However, if a database is formally encrypted, then the database contains only pseudorandom numbers, making it impossible to enable ML over it. In this project, we propose MLQENABLER (ML Queries Enabler) scheme to enable secure ML queries over encrypted database in cloud storage. MLQENABLER employs an index-aid approach to achieve security and ML capability simultaneously. Our initial experiments show that MLQENABLER achieves an acceptable security level while incurring only a slight ML performance degradation.
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme to enable secure machine learning queries over encrypted databases in cloud computing.
motivation: Cloud service providers cannot be fully trusted, so clients encrypt their data, but encrypted data prevents machine learning. The paper aims to enable ML on encrypted data.
method: The scheme uses an index-aid approach to allow ML queries on encrypted databases while maintaining security.
result: Initial experiments show acceptable security with slight ML performance degradation.
conclusion: The proposed scheme balances security and ML capability, but further work is needed.

title: Threshold Authorization Without Threshold Signatures: Signature-Agnostic Mpc Custody
authors: Dariia Porechna
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital-asset custody has been built on threshold multi-party approval: no operation proceeds unless [MATH] of [MATH] parties approve, and fewer than t compromised parties can neither authorize nor learn the authorization secret. Threshold signature schemes (TSS) have been the standard mechanism, but the post-quantum transition disrupts this model: standardized hash-based signatures resist efficient threshold signing, and lattice-based threshold protocols remain an emerging research track. We present a dual-gate architecture that separates member authentication from threshold authorization. Each member signs its approval with an ordinary signature under any EUF-CMA scheme; the quorum jointly produces a threshold seal from Shamir-shared secrets bound to the operation. The seal is the base instance of a programmable authorization computation: simple quorum is the minimal policy, while richer policies can evaluate secret-shared state without making the member-signature scheme part of that computation. The signature scheme is a deployment parameter: migrating from ECDSA to SLH-DSA or ML-DSA is a key rotation, not a protocol redesign, and members holding keys in commodity HSMs participate through the standard sign API. The architecture can be deployed wherever the asset-control path supports programmable verification, such as smart contracts, vault modules, or HSMs guarding a master key, and produces an enforcement-layer authorization rather than a native chain signature. Below-threshold secrecy is information-theoretic; an adversary holding [MATH] signing keys but no coefficient shares still cannot produce the seal.
tldr: A dual-gate architecture for threshold authorization in digital-asset custody that separates member authentication from threshold signing, enabling post-quantum signature agility.
motivation: Threshold signature schemes (TSS) face challenges with post-quantum signatures like hash-based and lattice-based schemes, which either resist efficient threshold signing or are not yet mature. The paper aims to provide a signature-agnostic authorization mechanism that can easily migrate between signature schemes.
method: The architecture uses ordinary signatures for member authentication and a threshold seal from Shamir-shared secrets for authorization, decoupling the signature scheme from the threshold logic. The seal is a programmable authorization computation that can implement various policies.
result: The architecture allows signature scheme migration via key rotation without protocol redesign, supports commodity HSMs, and provides information-theoretic secrecy below threshold.
conclusion: The proposed architecture offers a practical solution for post-quantum transition in digital-asset custody, but its focus is on applied cryptography and system design rather than quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Trace: A Two-Channel Robust Attribution Watermark Via Complementary Embeddings For LLM-Agent Trajectories
authors: Zheng Gao, Xiaoyu Li, Xiaoyan Feng, Jiaojiao Jiang, Yang Song, Yulei Sui, Zhenchang Xing, Liming Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents reach users through resellers, who may rebrand a developer's agent or substitute a cheaper model. When provenance is disputed, attribution rests on the trajectory log (the record of tool calls, observations, and executed actions, not the model's reasoning), which the reseller stores and processes to meter usage. A watermark must therefore survive an adversary with full read/write access to the very evidence it is detected from; existing agent watermarks do not, as their attribution is read straight off that log. We present TRACE, to our knowledge the first agent watermark that is distortion-free in its action choices, self-synchronizing under deletion, and unconditionally invariant under rewriting. Deletion desynchronizes a position-derived key and rewriting alters content, so a deletion-robust key must come from content and a rewrite-robust key from position, and no single key serves both. A trajectory, however, has room for two watermarks. TRACE superposes a selection channel that sets which action is chosen, keyed on local content with a distortion-free sampler, so the agent's distribution is provably unchanged and detection resynchronizes after deletions, and a tally channel that sets how many records each decision group holds, keyed on the log's skeleton alone, which no rewriting can touch. We prove this behavioral watermark's signal is bought with decision entropy, each decision paying at least half its entropy and deterministic decisions nothing, and that erasing both channels forces the reseller to corrupt the trajectories it resells. On ToolBench and ALFWorld, TRACE matches the unwatermarked agent's success rate while its selection channel reaches detection scores near z = 100 on long-horizon trajectories, stays detectable under 70% step deletion, and keeps a tally channel exactly unchanged under LLM rewriting of any strength.
tldr: This paper proposes a watermarking scheme for LLM agent trajectories that is robust to deletion and rewriting attacks.
motivation: Existing watermarks for LLM agents fail because resellers can modify the trajectory log, which is the only evidence for attribution. A robust watermark must survive full read/write access to the log.
method: TRACE uses two complementary channels: a selection channel that embeds a watermark via distortion-free action selection keyed on local content, and a tally channel that embeds a watermark via the number of records per decision group keyed on the log skeleton.
result: TRACE matches the unwatermarked agent's success rate, achieves detection scores near z=100 on long trajectories, remains detectable under 70% step deletion, and is invariant under LLM rewriting.
conclusion: TRACE is the first agent watermark that is distortion-free, self-synchronizing under deletion, and unconditionally invariant under rewriting, providing robust attribution for LLM agents.

title: Multi-Sender Bayesian Persuasion With Imperfect Information
authors: Andra Siva Sai Teja, Ganesh Ghalme, Sujit Gujar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a multi-sender Bayesian persuasion problem with one receiver and several strategic senders. The underlying ground state has multiple components, each privately observed by a different sender, while the receiver holds a common prior over the joint state space. Senders simultaneously choose signaling policies, and the receiver takes an action based on the posterior induced by the signals; each is sampled independently from the sender's signaling policy. We analyze the game induced by the receiver's straightforward policy, which selects a receiver-optimal action at every posterior. In particular, we characterize the senders' best responses under the straightforward policy and identify conditions on the prior that induce a fully informative equilibrium; i.e., truthfully reporting the ground truth is an equilibrium strategy for every sender. These conditions capture cases in which senders' incentives are sufficiently aligned to enable full revelation without additional commitment from the receiver. The important contribution of this paper is to analyze games induced by a more general (possibly randomized) class of action policies that the receiver commits to before senders choose their signaling strategies. We show that this commitment power fundamentally changes the problem. In particular, we show that for any prior over the joint state space, the receiver can construct action policies that maximize her payoff while ensuring a fully informative equilibrium.
tldr: This paper studies multi-sender Bayesian persuasion with imperfect information, focusing on equilibrium analysis and receiver commitment.
motivation: To understand how multiple strategic senders with private information can influence a receiver's decision through signaling, and how the receiver can design action policies to ensure full information revelation.
method: The authors model the problem as a game where senders choose signaling policies and the receiver commits to an action policy; they characterize conditions for fully informative equilibrium and construct optimal receiver policies.
result: They identify conditions on the prior that induce fully informative equilibrium under straightforward receiver policy, and show that with commitment, the receiver can always achieve a fully informative equilibrium.
conclusion: Receiver commitment power can fundamentally change the game, enabling full information revelation even when senders' incentives are not aligned.

title: Projected Incrementally Scattering Passive Systems On Closed Convex Sets
authors: Shantanu Singh, S\'ebastien Fueyo, George Weiss
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we show that the projected dynamical system obtained by restricting the state of an incrementally scattering passive system to a closed and convex subset K of the state space (a real Hilbert space), is also an incrementally scattering passive system. First we show that the projection of a maximal dissipative operator to the tangent cones of K is again maximal dissipative, hence, it determines a contraction semigroup.
tldr: This paper proves that projected dynamical systems on closed convex sets preserve incremental scattering passivity, a property from control theory.
motivation: To extend the theory of incrementally scattering passive systems to constrained state spaces, which is relevant for control of physical systems with constraints.
method: The authors show that the projection of a maximal dissipative operator onto tangent cones of a closed convex set remains maximal dissipative, and then use this to establish the passivity of the projected system.
result: The projected dynamical system is also incrementally scattering passive, and the associated contraction semigroup is characterized.
conclusion: The result provides a framework for analyzing passive systems with state constraints, with potential applications in control theory.

title: Algorithmic Expert Aggregation
authors: Hanrui Zhang Wei Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forecast aggregation aims to combine information from multiple Bayesian experts' forecasts into an aggregate forecast. In much of this literature, however, the aggregate forecast is optimized for a particular loss or robustness criterion and need not itself be calibrated with respect to the outcome. We introduce and study expert aggregation, where the goal is instead to aggregate Bayesian experts into a new expert that continues to provide calibrated forecasts. In particular, we consider a setting where each input expert reports calibrated predictions, and the aggregator observes the prior distribution over states, and the input experts, but not the underlying Bayes probabilities of the states. We ask whether one can (i) construct a calibrated output expert that Blackwell refines a target expert and cannot be further Blackwell improved using the available information; and (ii) when a proper loss is specified, compute a nearly loss-optimal expert among all such refinements. We formulate calibrated experts as reduced-form information structures and measure refinement by Blackwell dominance of the induced prediction distributions. We characterize the constructible output experts through observable linear information: the input experts generate a linear system whose row space determines which calibrated output predictions are identifiable, and a new expert is constructible exactly when its predictions lie in the associated observable nonnegative cone. We establish a sharp algorithmic picture. When randomized output experts are allowed, both questions above admit efficient algorithms. In contrast, deterministic output experts are computationally intractable: deciding whether a deterministic calibrated refinement exists is [MATH]-hard, and deterministic proper-loss optimization admits no multiplicative PTAS unless [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies algorithmic expert aggregation to produce calibrated forecasts, using Blackwell refinement and linear programming.
motivation: To combine forecasts from multiple Bayesian experts into a single calibrated forecast that is not just optimized for a loss function but also calibrated.
method: Formulates calibrated experts as reduced-form information structures and uses linear programming to characterize constructible output experts via observable linear information.
result: Randomized output experts can be efficiently constructed, but deterministic ones are computationally intractable (NP-hard).
conclusion: The paper provides a sharp algorithmic picture for expert aggregation with calibration constraints.

title: Theoretical Ab Initio Evolution Of Satellite Intensity Near Threshold For Cu K-shell Transitions
authors: Daniel Pinheiro, Gon\c{c}alo Baptista, C\'esar Godinho, Andr\'e Fernandes, Jorge Machado, Pedro Amaro, Nancy Paul, Martino Trassinelli, Miguel Avillez, Paul Indelicato, Jos\'e Paulo Santos, Mauro Guerra
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we have investigated the evolution of satellite intensity near the ionization threshold for Cu K-shell transitions through theoretical methods. Employing standard state-of-the-art ab initio methods, we have calculated all Cu K-shell transitions and simulated the full K[MATH] and K[MATH] spectrum where all transition parameters, as well as shake probabilities were determined theoretically. Through these calculations we show that standard state-of-the-art ab initio methods achieve good agreement with experiment and enable us to simulate the intensity evolution near ionization thresholds within a good margin of error. Below-threshold satellite intensity was found to originate from resonant 1s[MATH]3d and 1s[MATH]4p excitations in Cu(I) and Cu(II) oxide phases respectively, which were included in our simulations.
tldr: This paper uses ab initio methods to simulate satellite intensity evolution near the ionization threshold for Cu K-shell transitions.
motivation: Understanding satellite intensity near ionization thresholds is important for accurate X-ray spectroscopy, but the paper focuses on atomic physics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Standard state-of-the-art ab initio methods are employed to calculate all Cu K-shell transitions and simulate the full Kα and Kβ spectrum, including shake probabilities.
result: The simulations achieve good agreement with experiment, and below-threshold satellite intensity is attributed to resonant 1s→3d and 1s→4p excitations in Cu(I) and Cu(II) oxide phases.
conclusion: Standard ab initio methods can accurately simulate intensity evolution near ionization thresholds, but the work has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: The Periodic Table And The Group So(4,4): Ii. Double SO(4,2)-tower
authors: V. V. Varlamov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A group-theoretic interpretation of the periodic system of elements is given within the framework of the weight diagram of the Lie algebra [MATH] of the fourth rank, where the four quantum numbers [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], [MATH] correspond to the eigenvalues (weights) of the Cartan generators of the maximal Abelian subalgebra (the maximal torus of the group SO(4,4)). It is shown that the root system of the algebra [MATH] forms a regular four-dimensional self-dual polyhedron (24-cell). The action of the fourth Cartan generator associated with spin leads to a splitting of the Cartan-Weyl basis of the algebra [MATH] into two structurally identical bases, each of which is isomorphic to the Yao basis of the subalgebra [MATH] (the Lie algebra of the conformal group). At this point, a four-dimensional 24-cell is projected onto two three-dimensional cuboctahedra, each of which defines the root system of the subalgebra [MATH]. This splitting physically corresponds to spin doubling (two-valuedness). The structure of the energy levels of a periodic system is studied, the states of which (chemical elements) are represented as nodes of the weight diagram of the group algebra [MATH]. The structure of the double SO(4,2)-towers of Mendeleev, Seaborg, and 10-periodic extension is examined in detail. The period doubling associated with the sequence of period lengths 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, 32, [MATH] of the periodic system of elements is explained by the action of the fourth Cartan generator. It is shown that antimatter (Mendeleev anti-table consisting of antihydrogen, antihelium, antilitium, [MATH]) is naturally included in the general group-theoretic scheme of description of the periodic table.
tldr: This paper proposes a group-theoretic interpretation of the periodic table using the Lie algebra so(4,4) and its weight diagram, linking quantum numbers to Cartan generators and explaining period doubling via spin doubling.
motivation: The author aims to provide a unified mathematical framework for the periodic system of elements, including the structure of energy levels and the inclusion of antimatter, using higher-dimensional Lie algebras.
method: The paper uses the weight diagram of the Lie algebra so(4,4) to represent quantum numbers as eigenvalues of Cartan generators, and analyzes the root system as a 24-cell polyhedron, projecting onto two SO(4,2) subalgebras corresponding to spin doubling.
result: The study shows that the root system of so(4,4) forms a 24-cell, which splits into two cuboctahedra under spin doubling, and explains the sequence of period lengths (2,8,8,18,18,32,32,...) in the periodic table.
conclusion: The group-theoretic scheme naturally incorporates antimatter and provides a mathematical explanation for period doubling, suggesting a deeper symmetry underlying the periodic system.

title: Extracting Inter-nuclear Distances In The Oxygen Molecule Interacting With An XFEL-pulse: A Fundamental System For Understanding Coulomb Explosion Imaging
authors: Zixu Wang, Georgios Petros Katsoulis, Giorgio Visentin, Till Janke, Thomas Pfeifer, Agapi Emmanouilidou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08211v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the interaction of O[MATH] with an X-ray Free Electron laser (XFEL) pulse of short duration. We consider a photon energy of 570 eV, which allows for the formation of molecular states with up to two core holes. We compute the sum of the final kinetic energies, i.e. the kinetic energy release (KER) of the atomic fragments for different fragmentation channels. We demonstrate that with the knowledge of the potential energy curves the equilibrium inter-nuclear distance of O[MATH] is best extracted from the O[MATH]+O[MATH] channel and not from higher-charged channels such as O[MATH]+O[MATH]. This challenges our current understanding of Coulomb explosion imaging, where from just applying quasi-classical dynamics one expects that the equilibrium inter-nuclear distance of molecules is best extracted from higher-charged fragmentation channels. On the other hand, we show that the KER of the O[MATH]+O[MATH] channel is inconsistent with the one obtained by just calculating the Coulomb repulsion of the atomic fragments resulting from molecular dissociation.
tldr: This paper studies Coulomb explosion imaging of O2 molecules interacting with an XFEL pulse, focusing on extracting inter-nuclear distances from kinetic energy release.
motivation: Understanding Coulomb explosion imaging is important for molecular structure determination, but the paper's focus on a specific molecule and XFEL interaction does not align with the user's research interests.
method: The authors simulate the interaction of O2 with an XFEL pulse at 570 eV, compute kinetic energy release for different fragmentation channels, and compare with quasi-classical dynamics.
result: They find that the equilibrium inter-nuclear distance is best extracted from the O+ + O+ channel, contrary to the expectation that higher-charged channels are better.
conclusion: The results challenge current understanding of Coulomb explosion imaging, but the work is purely molecular physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: The Logistic-normal Integral And The Moments Of The Logistic-normal Distribution
authors: Dan Pirjol
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The logistic-normal integral appears in problems of statistical estimation for logistic models with Gaussian random effects, and generalized linear mixed models. We study the numerical evaluation of this integral and of its derivatives, and give closed form evaluations at certain points and series expansions. There is a continuum of possible series expansions, and we single out one series expansion which is optimal for numerical evaluation. We propose an algorithm for a precise numerical evaluation, based on the optimal series, with good approximation error control in the tails. As an application we give explicit results for the first two moments of a logistic-normal random variable.
tldr: This paper studies the numerical evaluation of the logistic-normal integral and its moments, with applications in statistical estimation.
motivation: The logistic-normal integral arises in logistic models with Gaussian random effects and generalized linear mixed models, but its numerical evaluation is challenging.
method: The authors derive series expansions for the integral and its derivatives, identify an optimal series for numerical evaluation, and propose an algorithm with error control.
result: Closed-form evaluations at certain points and an algorithm for precise numerical evaluation with good tail error control are provided, along with explicit results for the first two moments.
conclusion: The optimal series expansion enables accurate and efficient computation of logistic-normal integrals, useful for statistical applications.

title: Admissible Discrete Linear Propagators For High-Order Time Splittings Of Rotational Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equations With Arbitrary Three-Dimensional Rotation
authors: Fei Xue Tianqi Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study robust high-order time splittings for nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations whose linear part is defined by the Laplacian and an arbitrary three-dimensional rotation operator. After Fourier pseudospectral discretization, a continuous exact factorization of the linear flow need not yield a method self-adjoint fixed-grid propagator. For the original stage-wise explicit exact integrator, we identify a quadratic even term in the local logarithm and show that its visibility is state-dependent, so the observed temporal order of accuracy can depend on the initial data. We then formulate fixed-grid admissibility for discrete linear propagators and construct two admissible propagators for arbitrary three-dimensional rotation: a symmetrized explicit exact integrator and a palindromic generalized shear propagator. Both are unitary, first-order consistent, method self-adjoint, and have odd local logarithms. Numerical experiments verify the predicted defect mechanism and demonstrate recovery of the designed second-, fourth-, and sixth-order behavior with the admissible propagators.
tldr: This paper develops high-order time splitting methods for nonlinear Schrödinger equations with rotation, focusing on numerical analysis and propagator design.
motivation: To achieve high-order accuracy in time integration of rotating nonlinear Schrödinger equations, which are important in computational physics but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors identify a defect in standard explicit integrators due to a state-dependent quadratic term, then construct two admissible discrete linear propagators (symmetrized explicit exact integrator and palindromic generalized shear propagator) that are unitary, self-adjoint, and have odd local logarithms.
result: Numerical experiments verify the defect mechanism and demonstrate recovery of designed second-, fourth-, and sixth-order accuracy with the admissible propagators.
conclusion: The proposed admissible propagators enable robust high-order time splittings for rotating nonlinear Schrödinger equations, but the work is purely numerical and unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: RadioDiff-v2: Generative Angular Radio Maps For Multi-Beam Selection And Localization
authors: Xiucheng Wang, Junxi Huang, Nan Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Angular radio maps describe the received-power distribution over the angle of arrival and underpin beam selection and receiver localization in sixth-generation (6G) networks. Predicting the angular power spectrum (APS) from geometry is difficult, because the mapping is ill-posed in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions and must generalize to unseen environments. Distortion-minimizing regressors return the conditional mean, which over-smooths the spectrum and erases the multipath structure that downstream tasks need. We cast the task as a perception-distortion problem and propose RadioDiff-v2, a dual-branch one-dimensional diffusion transformer trained with flow matching. It couples periodic angular encoding, adaptive layer-normalization conditioning, a Fourier angular mixer, and joint velocity and clean-signal heads. A per-metric estimator portfolio reads every deployment quantity from this single model, so that samples carry the distribution, the clean-signal head supplies a regression-grade point estimate, Bayes-optimal rules select beams, and the conditional likelihood localizes the receiver. We prove that a concentrated conditional yields a straight probability-flow trajectory that one step integrates exactly, identifying deterministic transport as the correct inductive bias. On a zero-shot test of 99 environments and one million links, RadioDiff-v2 leads every baseline on every metric, with a 0.39 dB Wasserstein-1 distance, per-bin error below the regression baseline, a 2.43 dB eight-beam NLOS sweep loss, and a 20.6-pixel localization error with four base stations. Code is available at [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes a generative diffusion model for predicting angular radio maps to aid beam selection and localization in 6G networks.
motivation: Accurate angular power spectrum prediction is challenging in NLOS conditions, and existing regressors over-smooth the spectrum, losing multipath structure needed for downstream tasks.
method: RadioDiff-v2 uses a dual-branch one-dimensional diffusion transformer with flow matching, periodic angular encoding, adaptive layer normalization, and joint velocity and clean-signal heads to generate angular radio maps.
result: On zero-shot tests across 99 environments and one million links, RadioDiff-v2 outperforms all baselines, achieving 0.39 dB Wasserstein-1 distance, 2.43 dB eight-beam NLOS sweep loss, and 20.6-pixel localization error.
conclusion: The generative approach preserves multipath structure and enables accurate beam selection and localization from a single model, demonstrating strong generalization to unseen environments.

title: Sharp Spectral Bounds For Symmetric Positive Definite Tensors Via Multiple Algebraic Invariants
authors: Hemant Sharma, Snigdhashree Nayak, Ankit Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the trace--determinant framework of Nayak, Sharma, and Mishra~ for bounding the H-eigenvalues of symmetric positive definite tensors. First, we replace the Arithmetic--Geometric Mean (AM--GM) relaxation underlying previous bounds by the exact solution of the associated constrained optimization problem, yielding sharp upper and lower bounds that are attained on the admissible spectral variety. Second, we incorporate higher-order power sums as additional spectral invariants and prove a structural theorem showing that any extremizer over a [MATH]-invariant feasibility region has at most [MATH] distinct spectral values. This reduces the problem to a finite collection of low-dimensional polynomial systems and yields a hierarchy of increasingly tight bounds. For the four-invariant case [MATH], we develop a complete theory including solution-count estimates, a multistart Newton algorithm, and sharpness conditions. We also derive closed-form bounds in small dimensions, establish perturbation estimates, and obtain refined Lyapunov region-of-attraction bounds. Numerical experiments for dimensions up to [MATH] show that the sharp three-invariant bound reduces the median relative overestimation gap from [MATH] to [MATH] while maintaining low computational cost. The framework is validated on tensors with real H-spectrum.
tldr: This paper presents sharp spectral bounds for symmetric positive definite tensors using multiple algebraic invariants.
motivation: Improving eigenvalue bounds for tensors is important for applications like stability analysis, but the paper focuses on pure algebraic methods without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors replace the AM-GM relaxation with exact constrained optimization and incorporate higher-order power sums as invariants, reducing the problem to solving low-dimensional polynomial systems.
result: The three-invariant bound reduces the median relative overestimation gap from 30% to 5% for dimensions up to 10, with low computational cost.
conclusion: The framework provides a hierarchy of increasingly tight bounds validated on tensors with real H-spectrum, but has no relevance to quantum information theory or related fields.

title: A Study Of Skew-Polycyclic Codes Over A Non-Chain Ring
authors: Seema Antil, Seema Chahal, Manju Khan, Sugandha Maheshwary
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a prime \(p\) and a positive integer \(m\), let \(_{p^m}\) be the finite field of cardinality \(p^m\), and let [MATH] be a finite non-chain ring. In this paper, we study skew polycyclic codes of length \(lj\) associated with \(f(x)^j\), where \(f(x)\) is a central polynomial of degree \(l\) in [MATH] where [MATH] being an automorphism of \(R_{u^2,v^2,p^m}\). We describe these codes, characterize free skew polycyclic codes, and determine their ranks. Under suitable centrality assumptions, we decompose the quotient ring associated with \(x^{np^s}-\lambda\), where \(\gcd(n,p)=1\) and \(\Theta(\lambda)=\lambda\). This reduces the study of skew \((\lambda,\Theta)\)-constacyclic codes of length \(np^s\) to the study of left ideals of [MATH] where \(f(x)\) is a central irreducible divisor of degree \(l\) of \(x^{np^s}-\lambda\), for an invertible element \(\lambda\in R_{u^2,v^2,p^m}\) and \(j\in\). We then apply these results to skew \((\lambda,\Theta)\)-constacyclic codes of length \(p^s\) for different classes of units \(\lambda\). Several examples are presented to illustrate the theory and to obtain optimal codes. Finally, when \(\Theta\) is the identity automorphism, we study constacyclic codes of length \(np^s\) over \(R_{u^2,v^2,p^m}\), according as \(x^n-\alpha_0\) is irreducible or reducible over \(_{p^m}\). These results extend the work of and on constacyclic codes of length \(np^s\) over \(_{p^m}+u_{p^m}\) to the finite non-chain ring \(R_{u^2,v^2,p^m}\).
tldr: This paper studies skew polycyclic codes over a non-chain ring, extending algebraic coding theory results.
motivation: To generalize constacyclic codes to skew polycyclic codes over a specific non-chain ring, building on previous work.
method: Uses algebraic methods: central polynomials, automorphisms, quotient ring decompositions, and classification of free codes.
result: Characterizes free skew polycyclic codes, determines their ranks, and reduces skew constacyclic codes to left ideals under centrality assumptions.
conclusion: Provides theoretical extensions and examples of optimal codes, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Building Confidence Regions For Reeb Graphs Using The Interleaving Distance
authors: Matteo Pegoraro, Alberto Conforti, Mathieu Carri\`ere
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop confidence regions for Reeb graphs from finite samples using the interleaving distance. Given a point cloud equipped with a filter function, we construct a finite proximity graph, extend the filter linearly, and use the Reeb cosheaf of the resulting filtered graph as the primary estimator. Mapper graphs are then treated as controlled cover-based coarsenings of this estimator, separating the statistical approximation problem from the visualization problem. We prove stability bounds for the Reeb estimators obtained both using intrinsic and extrinsic metrics, the latter under positive-reach assumptions, and derive interleaving-distance confidence regions from either \((a,b)\)-standard sampling assumptions or subsampling-based Hausdorff scale estimates. We also compare this object-level metric viewpoint with persistence-based guarantees by showing that the extended-persistence pseudometric is bounded by twice the interleaving distance, with sharp constant \(1\) for the \(H_0\)-related components. Numerical experiments illustrate how statistically significant features can be identified and then projected to Mapper graphs for interpretation.
tldr: This paper develops confidence regions for Reeb graphs using the interleaving distance, focusing on topological data analysis.
motivation: Reeb graphs are used in topological data analysis but lack statistical guarantees; the paper aims to provide confidence regions for features extracted from finite samples.
method: The authors construct a Reeb cosheaf estimator from a filtered proximity graph and treat Mapper graphs as coarsenings, proving stability bounds and deriving confidence regions from sampling assumptions or subsampling.
result: They show that the extended-persistence pseudometric is bounded by twice the interleaving distance, with a sharp constant for H0-related components, and demonstrate identification of statistically significant features in numerical experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a statistical framework for Reeb graphs, enabling robust feature identification and visualization via Mapper graphs.

title: Who Broke The System? Failure Localization In LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Yufei Xia, Anjun Gao, Yueyang Quan, Zhuqing Liu, Minghong Fang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems enable complex problem solving through coordinated reasoning and action, but their distributed structure also introduces new challenges in diagnosing system-level failures. When an execution fails, identifying which agent is responsible and at what point the trajectory first becomes irreversibly misdirected is difficult due to long-horizon interactions and tightly coupled agent behaviors. In this paper, we study the problem of failure localization in LLM-based multi-agent systems and present AgentLocate, a framework that attributes failures to both a specific agent and the earliest decisive step. AgentLocate combines an LLM-based judging mechanism with multi-perspective verification by independent evaluators, whose assessments are aggregated using a confidence-aware strategy. The resulting feedback is further used to adapt the judge through lightweight fine-tuning, improving attribution quality. We evaluate AgentLocate on two complementary benchmarks covering diverse tasks, agent configurations, and trajectory lengths. Experimental results show that AgentLocate consistently outperforms existing failure localization methods in identifying both responsible agents and failure steps, while remaining efficient in terms of token usage and running time.
tldr: This paper presents a framework for failure localization in LLM-based multi-agent systems, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: Diagnosing failures in LLM-based multi-agent systems is challenging due to long-horizon interactions and tightly coupled agent behaviors.
method: AgentLocate combines an LLM-based judging mechanism with multi-perspective verification by independent evaluators, aggregated via a confidence-aware strategy, and adapts the judge through lightweight fine-tuning.
result: AgentLocate outperforms existing methods in identifying responsible agents and failure steps while being efficient in token usage and running time.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively localizes failures in LLM-based multi-agent systems.

title: Securing Autonomous Vehicle Systems Via Twin-Aware Federated Reinforcement Learning
authors: Zifan Zhang, Minghong Fang, Dianwei Chen, Zhuqing Liu, Prashant Khanduri, Xianfeng Yang, Anupam Das, Yuchen Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated reinforcement learning (FRL) is crucial for enabling collaborative learning across multiple agents without sharing raw data, thereby enhancing privacy and scalability in the decision-making process within dynamic vehicular environments. However, poisoning attacks pose a significant threat to the security and reliability of FRL-based systems, particularly in safety-critical autonomous driving, where this vulnerability remains largely unexplored. These attacks can compromise the global control model by subtly injecting malicious system parameters, leading to potential hazards. To counter these challenges, we present \alg (ure ggregation with oisoning-revention and historical reinforcement) as a defensive framework aimed at enhancing the robustness of FRL systems designed for safety-critical driving scenarios. \alg strategically integrates digital twins for rehearsal-based learning and leverages historical aggregated model parameters along with a selected central gradient to ensure that only benign data is aggregated, effectively mitigating the influence of malicious agents. Theoretical guarantees are provided for the convergence performance of \alg in the presence of poisoning attacks. We also validate the effectiveness of \alg using developed digital twins that model realistic highway environments to evaluate the control of autonomous vehicles under adversarial conditions.
tldr: This paper proposes a federated reinforcement learning framework with digital twins to defend against poisoning attacks in autonomous vehicle systems.
motivation: Poisoning attacks threaten the security of federated reinforcement learning in safety-critical autonomous driving, and existing defenses are insufficient.
method: The framework integrates digital twins for rehearsal-based learning and uses historical aggregated model parameters with a central gradient to filter malicious updates.
result: Theoretical convergence guarantees are provided, and simulations on realistic highway environments demonstrate effectiveness against adversarial conditions.
conclusion: The proposed method enhances robustness of FRL systems against poisoning attacks, improving safety in autonomous driving.

title: From Legacy Documentation To Oscal: An MCP-Based Agent Pipeline For Threat-Informed Continuous Compliance In Critical Infrastructure
authors: Marian Margraf Lea Roxanne Muth
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In critical infrastructure, operational technology environments often cannot be actively scanned, and yet active system feedback is needed for risk assessment and compliance. This paper presents a non-invasive, MCP-grounded multi-agent pipeline that converts natural-language system descriptions into source-verified knowledge graph and audit-ready artifacts in the NIST OSCAL format for continuous automated compliance management. The architecture decouples LLM-based reasoning from deterministic knowledge retrieval against authoritative threat-intelligence sources, reducing the risk of fabricated vulnerabilities and hallucinated attack paths. In an evidence-based synthetic scenario of a water utility, the pipeline achieves 0.90 CVE recall and perfect D3FEND recall. It generates a schema-valid OSCAL System Security Plan and an OSCAL Security Assessment Report. Nevertheless, the core insight is not that grounding via MCP eliminates errors (e.g., hallucinations) entirely from the pipeline, but that it shifts errors into the first phase of asset extraction from the natural language description. Here, a single incorrectly extracted entity can lead to genuine but irrelevant CVEs in subsequent stages of the pipeline, which consumes time and resources. However, it makes the remaining risk visible, verifiable, and suitable for a time-efficient manual review, since the infrastructure (e.g., version numbers, OS, etc.) is typically known.
tldr: This paper presents an MCP-based multi-agent pipeline for converting natural-language system descriptions into OSCAL compliance artifacts for critical infrastructure.
motivation: Operational technology environments in critical infrastructure cannot be actively scanned, yet require risk assessment and compliance. The authors aim to provide a non-invasive method to generate audit-ready artifacts from legacy documentation.
method: The pipeline uses LLM-based reasoning decoupled from deterministic knowledge retrieval against threat-intelligence sources, converting natural-language descriptions into a knowledge graph and OSCAL-format documents.
result: In a synthetic water utility scenario, the pipeline achieves 0.90 CVE recall and perfect D3FEND recall, generating schema-valid OSCAL System Security Plan and Security Assessment Report.
conclusion: The approach shifts errors to the asset extraction phase, making remaining risk visible and verifiable for manual review, though it does not eliminate hallucinations entirely.

title: Secure Qr Codes: Authenticity Verification Via EdDSA Signatures And Cbor Certificates
authors: Wojciech Wodo Wojciech Jonderko
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: QR codes are a ubiquitous part of daily life, widely trusted by millions. However, their lack of inherent security features has given rise to critical attack vectors, such as spoofing (quishing) on public infrastructure like self-service parking machines. To address this, we present a comprehensive evolution of secure QR code architectures. First, we evaluate a fully offline proof-of-concept leveraging EdDSA signatures (instantiated on the Ed25519 curve), CBOR-encoded certificates, and ZLIB compression, demonstrating that robust cryptographic integrity can be achieved within the QR code's strict static capacity. However, recognizing the scalability limitations of fully offline models-specifically the inability to perform immediate key revocation in massive smart-city IoT deployments-we subsequently propose a scalable Hybrid Web PKI architecture. This forward-looking model utilizes standardized JWKS endpoints, a Central Trust Registry, and URL fragments to ensure seamless backward compatibility with standard native cameras while providing dynamic, real-time validation for compliant applications. This dual-mode approach offers a practical, deployable path toward eliminating QR spoofing.
tldr: This paper proposes cryptographic enhancements to QR codes using EdDSA signatures and CBOR certificates to prevent spoofing.
motivation: QR codes lack inherent security, making them vulnerable to spoofing attacks in public infrastructure.
method: The authors design an offline proof-of-concept using EdDSA signatures and CBOR certificates, and a hybrid web PKI architecture for scalable key revocation.
result: The offline model achieves cryptographic integrity within QR code capacity; the hybrid model enables dynamic validation.
conclusion: The dual-mode approach provides a practical path to eliminate QR spoofing while maintaining backward compatibility.

title: On Constructing Most General Solutions For Parametric Constraints (Extended Preprint)
authors: Viorica Sofronie-Stokkermans
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be a theory allowing a form of elimination of existential quantifiers (possibly for formulae in a certain class). We analyze possibilities of constructing (most general) solutions w.r.t.\ [MATH] for formulae of the form [MATH], where [MATH] is a quantifier-free conjunction of literals in the signature of [MATH], and the free variables [MATH] are regarded as parameters. We show that in the presence of function symbols which describe ``{\sf if}-{\sf then}-{\sf else}'' constructions in certain models of [MATH], we can describe the most general solution of such formulae, thus generalizing results about the existence of most general unifiers in discriminator varieties. We illustrate the ideas on examples.
tldr: This paper presents a method for constructing most general solutions to parametric constraints in first-order theories with quantifier elimination, generalizing results on most general unifiers in discriminator varieties.
motivation: The paper aims to extend the theory of most general unifiers to a broader class of theories by leveraging quantifier elimination and if-then-else functions.
method: The authors analyze parametric constraint formulae and show that in theories with if-then-else function symbols, the most general solution can be described, generalizing known results.
result: They provide a constructive description of most general solutions for parametric constraints in such theories, illustrated with examples.
conclusion: The work contributes to automated reasoning and algebraic logic but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: TRM-Raft: A Byzantine-Resistant Raft Consensus Via Integrated Trust And Reputation Model
authors: Jie Zhang, Xubo Fan, Xiaohong Li, Zhiyong Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internetware envisions autonomous software entities collaborating over the open Internet. Raft consensus is widely adopted for its simplicity and performance in distributed coordination, e.g., service registries and blockchains. However, Raft assumes crash faults only, making it vulnerable to Byzantine behaviors like election forgery and log tampering. Existing BFT protocols incur high overhead, while ad-hoc hardening lacks unified defense. We propose , a Byzantine-resistant enhancement that non-intrusively integrates a Blockchain-based Trust and Reputation Model (B-TRM) into the consensus core. It quantifies multi-dimensional node behaviors, applies adaptive penalties distinguishing accidental faults from malice, and embeds reputation into leader election and log replication. A reputation-aware election penalizes term/index forgery, excluding low-reputation nodes from leadership. A Schnorr-signature-based mechanism lets followers verify log integrity; tampering triggers reputation decay and leader replacement. Evaluated on Hyperledger Fabric in a realistic Internetware setting, TRM-Raft keeps malicious leader ratio below 5\% even with 40\% Byzantine nodes, with <10\% throughput loss and <5\% latency increase over vanilla Raft. TRM-Raft offers a lightweight, practical trustworthiness path for Internetware systems relying on Raft.
tldr: This paper proposes a Byzantine-resistant enhancement to the Raft consensus protocol using a blockchain-based trust and reputation model.
motivation: Raft consensus is vulnerable to Byzantine behaviors like election forgery and log tampering, and existing BFT protocols are too heavy for Internetware systems.
method: The authors integrate a Blockchain-based Trust and Reputation Model (B-TRM) into Raft, using reputation-aware leader election and Schnorr-signature-based log integrity verification.
result: TRM-Raft keeps malicious leader ratio below 5% even with 40% Byzantine nodes, with less than 10% throughput loss and less than 5% latency increase over vanilla Raft.
conclusion: TRM-Raft offers a lightweight, practical trustworthiness path for Internetware systems relying on Raft.
