title: From Rules To Nash Equilibria: A Lean 4 Case Study In Game-Theoretic Analysis Of A Competitive Trading Card Game
authors: Tulio Soria Arthur F. Ramos
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a metagame analysis of the competitive Pokemon Trading Card Game, machine-checked in Lean 4 over real tournament data. The headline game-theoretic results, including Nash equilibrium, replicator dynamics, and the matrix-level type-bridge computation, rely on native_decide, which trusts Lean's compiler rather than its kernel; the trust boundary is made explicit. The artifact spans approximately 31,900 lines, 87 files, and 2,627 theorems, of which roughly 200 directly verify empirical claims, with no sorry, admit, or custom axioms. Analyzing Trainer Hill data from January to February 2026 for events with at least 50 players, over 14 archetypes and their full pairwise matchup matrix, we prove a popularity paradox: the most played deck, Dragapult, with 15.5% metagame share, has only 46.7% expected win rate, while Grimmsnarl, with 5.1% share, achieves 52.7%. A machine-checked Nash equilibrium of the raw game assigns Dragapult 0% weight; exhaustive enumeration over all nonempty support subsets confirms a unique symmetric Nash equilibrium of the constant-sum symmetrization with seven-deck support. Against this equilibrium mix, Dragapult falls 40.4 permil below the game value. Single-step replicator dynamics indicate downward fitness pressure on Dragapult, upward pressure on Grimmsnarl, and strongest extinction pressure on Alakazam. A 10,000-iteration sensitivity analysis confirms qualitative stability, with core support decks appearing in more than 96% of resampled equilibria. The primary contribution is methodological: a reproducible case study showing how formal verification can turn qualitative metagame narratives into machine-checkable, re-runnable strategic science.
tldr: This paper uses Lean 4 to formally verify game-theoretic analysis of a competitive trading card game, focusing on Nash equilibria and replicator dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to demonstrate how formal verification can make qualitative metagame narratives rigorous and reproducible.
method: They formalize matchup matrices, compute Nash equilibria via exhaustive enumeration, and run replicator dynamics and sensitivity analysis, all machine-checked in Lean 4.
result: They find a popularity paradox and a unique symmetric Nash equilibrium with seven-deck support, and show qualitative stability of core decks.
conclusion: The work is a methodological case study for applying formal verification to strategic game analysis, but it does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Invariance Audits For Quantum Kernels And Variational Rewinding: A Real-to-Hermitian Taxonomy Of Projector, Flag, Anchor, And Density Geometry
authors: Azadeh Alavi, Fatemeh Kouchmeshki, Hossein Akhoundi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine-learning models often replace vectors by normalized directions, projectors, covariances, subspaces, ordered flags, quantum states, or density operators before any classifier is fitted. This replacement is an invariance decision: it determines which distinctions are kept and which are quotiented out. We develop a self-contained real-to-Hermitian taxonomy for auditing such representations in quantum machine learning. On the real side, we formalize Grassmann and flag projector kernels, prove positive semidefiniteness and block-gauge invariance of a weighted flag kernel, and give a same-span block-swap witness showing when whole-span Grassmann geometry must fail while ordered flags succeed. On the quantum side, we prove that a noiseless fidelity kernel is exactly the Hilbert--Schmidt inner product between the associated rank-one Hermitian projectors, and that a QVR-style return probability is exactly an overlap score between the input projector and a learned anchor operator. Rank-constrained returns correspond to complex Grassmann anchors, while mixed or multimodal class models are naturally represented by density or positive-semidefinite anchors. Controlled vector, subspace, statevector, anomaly, finite-shot, and quotient-witness experiments support the same conclusion: quantum and geometric lifts are useful when their invariances match the task, and fail correctly when discarded information is label-bearing. The paper makes no hardware-speedup or quantum-advantage claim.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Ultra-high-speed Chemiluminescence Tomography Of Spinning-mode Detonation Waves
authors: Amit K. Singh, Mateo Gomez, Kevin Y. Cho, Aaron W. Skiba, Samuel J. Grauer
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents a chemiluminescence tomography campaign to reconstruct time-resolved, three-dimensional reacting structures in detonation waves propagating through ethylene-based mixtures at 1 atm. Images of chemiluminescence are recorded simultaneously by five cameras through a cylindrical sapphire test section, and a custom calibration procedure is developed to account for refraction through the cylinder. The images are combined to reconstruct an effective emission source term field at megahertz rates. Reconstructions are reported for a persistent spinning detonation, a failed spinning detonation, and a case with counter-propagating transverse fronts. The reconstructed fields enable visualization of wave morphologies, determination of the axial and azimuthal wave speeds, and estimation of key geometric and kinematic parameters. These results demonstrate time-resolved chemiluminescence tomography as a non-intrusive tool for resolving volumetric detonation dynamics that are difficult to infer from point, planar, or line-of-sight diagnostics.
tldr: This paper presents a chemiluminescence tomography technique for visualizing spinning-mode detonation waves in ethylene-based mixtures.
motivation: Detonation dynamics are difficult to infer from point or planar diagnostics; a non-intrusive volumetric imaging method is needed.
method: Five cameras simultaneously capture chemiluminescence through a cylindrical sapphire test section; a custom calibration accounts for refraction, and an effective emission source term field is reconstructed at megahertz rates.
result: Reconstructions of persistent and failed spinning detonations, as well as counter-propagating fronts, enable visualization of wave morphologies and estimation of wave speeds and geometric parameters.
conclusion: Time-resolved chemiluminescence tomography is demonstrated as a tool for resolving volumetric detonation dynamics.

title: A Puck-informed Mode-resolved Phase-field Fatigue Framework For Unidirectional Composites
authors: Aamir Dean
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fatigue fracture in unidirectional fibre-reinforced composites is strongly mode dependent: transverse and off-axis cycling is governed by matrix and inter-fibre mechanisms, whereas fibre-aligned cycling activates a longitudinal channel with a higher fracture-energy scale and a different crack topology. Single-damage-variable models can fit global stiffness loss but cannot identify the active mechanism. This work proposes a Puck-informed, mode-resolved phase-field fatigue framework with separate channels for fibre-dominated and matrix/inter-fibre fatigue. Each channel has its own fatigue history, threshold, and resistance-degradation law. Fatigue does not directly degrade elastic stiffness; it lowers the fracture resistance of the active channel, while the corresponding phase field controls stiffness loss and crack-path evolution. The formulation is implemented in Abaqus/Standard using a compact UMAT-UEL architecture with one orthotropic mechanical routine and two scalar phase-field layers. Using one fixed IM7/8552 material and fatigue card, the model is verified through one-element tests, parameter sweeps, and centred-notch and open-hole tension cases at 0, 45, and 90 degrees under monotonic and cyclic loading. Without orientation- or geometry-specific tuning, the framework reproduces transverse matrix/inter-fibre cracking at 90 degrees, off-axis cracking at 45 degrees, and longitudinal matrix splitting with delayed fibre activation at 0 degrees. The fatigue lives follow the expected ordering: 45- and 90-degree cases fail within about 1,000 cycles, while 0-degree cases run out to 200,000 cycles without fibre cracking. Additional load, hole-size, mesh, length-scale, and cycle-block studies confirm consistent crack modes and converged trends. The study is a numerical verification and cross-geometry consistency assessment, not a calibrated experimental life-prediction claim.
tldr: A phase-field fatigue framework for unidirectional composites using Puck's criterion, with separate damage channels for fiber and matrix modes.
motivation: Existing single-damage-variable models cannot distinguish between fiber-dominated and matrix fatigue mechanisms in composites.
method: The framework implements two scalar phase-field layers with independent fatigue histories and resistance degradation laws, coupled with orthotropic elasticity in Abaqus.
result: The model reproduces expected crack modes and fatigue life ordering for different fiber orientations without orientation-specific tuning.
conclusion: The framework provides a consistent numerical tool for mode-resolved fatigue analysis, but requires experimental calibration for predictive use.

title: Parallel Simulation Of Rarefied Gas Flows On Unstructured Meshes Using The DIG-augmented Dsmc Method
authors: Tao Huang, Liyan Luo, Hong Deng, Lei Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While the direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) is a mainstream stochastic particle method for simulating rarefied gas flows, it incurs excessively high computational costs in the near continuum regime. As a hybrid acceleration approach coupling DSMC with macroscopic synthetic equations, the direct intermittent general synthetic iterative scheme (DIG) delivers fast convergence and asymptotic-preserving characteristics, which effectively alleviate the kinetic scale limitations inherent to standard DSMC. In this study, we develop a parallel DIG augmented DSMC solver for three dimensional rarefied gas flow simulations on unstructured meshes. On top of the standard DSMC algorithms for particle transport and collisions, a reliable intermittent coupling framework is constructed to exchange macroscopic flow data between the stochastic DSMC module and deterministic macroscopic synthetic equations. For parallel execution on unstructured grids, we employ a hybrid MPI architecture equipped with ghost cells to enable local particle tracking and batch inter-rank particle migration. A graph partitioning based dynamic load balancing strategy is also integrated to mitigate uneven particle distribution over computational domains. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed solver achieves satisfactory agreement with the SPARTA DSMC. Leveraging the fast convergence and asymptotic-preserving properties of the DIG method, the required number of spatial cells and statistical sampling steps are drastically decreased, leading to substantial reductions in computational memory and runtime. This work presents an efficient high-performance numerical tool for high-fidelity simulations of rarefied flows over complex geometries. The code is available in the developer repository at the github link.
tldr: This paper presents a parallel implementation of the DIG-augmented DSMC method for rarefied gas flow simulations on unstructured meshes.
motivation: Standard DSMC is computationally expensive in the near-continuum regime; the DIG method accelerates convergence but lacks a parallel implementation for complex geometries.
method: A hybrid MPI architecture with ghost cells and dynamic load balancing is developed to couple DSMC with macroscopic synthetic equations on unstructured grids.
result: The solver achieves good agreement with SPARTA DSMC while drastically reducing computational memory and runtime.
conclusion: The work provides an efficient high-performance tool for rarefied gas flow simulations over complex geometries.

title: Tree-based Solution Representations For Quadratic Bilinear Systems And Their Consequences In Model Order Reduction
authors: Martin Redmann
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate quadratic bilinear systems by developing novel tree-based representations of their solutions. The proposed framework decomposes the solution into a sequence of coupled bilinear subsystems whose components admit explicit expansions indexed by full binary trees. These representations yield sufficient conditions for the existence of global solutions and lead to new output bounds in terms of reachability Gramians. Motivated by these estimates, we introduce time-limited and infinite-horizon reachability and observability Gramians, establish sufficient conditions for their existence, and characterize them through nonlinear matrix equations. The associated Gramians are employed to identify dominant state-spaces and to derive exact reduced-order models obtained by removing Gramian kernels. Building on these results, we develop a balanced truncation method for quadratic bilinear systems and prove an error bound for the reduced-order approximation. The proposed framework provides a unified connection between tree-based solution representations, nonlinear Gramian theory, and balanced truncation for quadratic bilinear systems, closing several theoretical gaps in the analysis of Gramian-based model reduction for this class of systems.
tldr: This paper develops tree-based solution representations and Gramian-based model order reduction for quadratic bilinear systems, which are unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Quadratic bilinear systems arise in control theory and model reduction, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors propose tree-based expansions for solutions, define reachability and observability Gramians, and derive a balanced truncation method with error bounds.
result: Sufficient conditions for global solutions and new output bounds are obtained, along with exact reduced-order models by removing Gramian kernels.
conclusion: The framework unifies tree-based representations, nonlinear Gramian theory, and balanced truncation for quadratic bilinear systems, but has no relevance to the user's research interests.

title: Combining Cusped Triangle Groups With Blaschke Products: Commensurable Matings
authors: Yusheng Luo, Mahan Mj, Sabyasachi Mukherjee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we construct algebraic correspondences as matings of Fuchsian [MATH]-triangle groups with Blaschke products. Combined with the results of [MM25], this proves mateability of all cusped triangle groups with suitable Blaschke products. The proof of the main result involves associating two piecewise analytic circle maps to the [MATH]triangle group, mating these maps with appropriate Blaschke products to produce two commensurable conformal matings, and finally constructing the desired algebraic correspondence as a common lift of the two conformal matings.
tldr: This paper constructs algebraic correspondences by mating Fuchsian triangle groups with Blaschke products, a result in complex dynamics and geometry.
motivation: The authors aim to prove mateability of all cusped triangle groups with suitable Blaschke products, extending previous work.
method: They associate piecewise analytic circle maps to the triangle group, mate these maps with Blaschke products to produce two commensurable conformal matings, and then construct the desired algebraic correspondence as a common lift.
result: The main result is the construction of algebraic correspondences as matings, proving mateability for all cusped triangle groups with appropriate Blaschke products.
conclusion: This work contributes to the theory of algebraic correspondences and complex dynamics, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: On The Approximation Of Optimal Control In Regime-Switching Diffusions
authors: Dinesh Rathia Somnath Pradhan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study approximation and structural simplification of optimal control policies for controlled regime-switching diffusion processes for discounted, ergodic, finite-horizon, and exit-time criteria. We first establish continuity of the cost functionals over classes of Markov and stationary Markov policies by exploiting elliptic and parabolic regularity of the corresponding Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman and Poisson equations. Using density results of policies with finite-action, piecewise-constant, and Lipschitz continuous, we show that each control problem admits [MATH]-optimal policies within these structured subclasses. We then construct an Euler--Maruyama approximation of the controlled regime-switching diffusion under piecewise-constant controls. We prove strong convergence of the controlled state process and establish convergence of the associated finite-horizon value functions with rate [MATH]. Building on this discretization, we develop a finite-state approximation of the induced discrete-time Markov chain via state-space quantization. We show that the value functions of the finite models converge uniformly on compact sets to the value function of the original problem, and that optimal policies of the approximating models are asymptotically optimal. These results provide a systematic framework for approximating regime-switching diffusion control problems and justify the use of structured policies and finite-state models for numerical implementation.
tldr: This paper studies optimal control approximation for regime-switching diffusions, a topic in stochastic control theory with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to simplify and approximate optimal control policies for regime-switching diffusion processes, which are used in finance and engineering.
method: It uses elliptic and parabolic regularity of HJB equations, density results for structured policies, Euler-Maruyama discretization, and state-space quantization.
result: It proves existence of epsilon-optimal policies in structured subclasses, strong convergence of the discretized state process, and uniform convergence of value functions.
conclusion: The results provide a systematic framework for numerical implementation of regime-switching diffusion control problems.

title: Empirical Comparison Of Unified Benders Cuts For Multi-Commodity Fixed-Charge Network Design
authors: Eric Larsen, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Cordeau, Antonio Frangioni, Emma Frejinger
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Among the many types of acceleration techniques designed to improve the performance of Benders decomposition, unified cut generation schemes have recently attracted a keen interest. Unified cuts aim for a better balance between the generation of optimality and feasibility cuts, while also providing a way to compare the strengths of different feasibility cuts. Our goal is to assess the experimental performance of a broad selection of unified and distinct Benders cuts in the context of the multi-commodity fixed-charge network design problem (MCFNDP). We express under a common mathematical structure and notation the construction of each unified or distinct Benders cut considered. We also explain how the generic formulations of the Benders cuts can be specialized to conform to the specifications of the MCFNDP. In addition, we suggest bespoke methods for comparing the performance of several solution methods when the benchmark is made up of heterogeneous problem instances. We report the results of a systematic empirical analysis comparing the performances of 50 Benders methods involving unified or distinct cuts in applications to a common testing bench made up of standardized MCFNDP instances. The analysis identifies a small number of leading Benders methods, namely those featuring the static Brandenberg-Stursberg cuts and the Hosseini-Turner l1-deepest cuts. In addition, we also report results obtained by using both Gurobi and CPLEX as the supporting solver to the SMS++ computation library.
tldr: This paper empirically compares unified Benders cuts for the multi-commodity fixed-charge network design problem, a topic in operations research.
motivation: Benders decomposition is a classical optimization technique; unified cuts aim to improve its performance, but the paper focuses on a specific network design problem with no quantum or thermodynamic content.
method: The authors formulate various Benders cuts under a common structure, specialize them to the MCFNDP, and test 50 methods on standardized instances using Gurobi and CPLEX.
result: A small number of leading methods are identified, including static Brandenberg-Stursberg cuts and Hosseini-Turner l1-deepest cuts.
conclusion: The study provides a systematic empirical comparison and identifies the most effective Benders cut variants for the MCFNDP.

title: On Cube And Cremona Rigidity For Higher-rank Lattices
authors: Shengyuan Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For irreducible lattices in semisimple Lie groups of real rank at least [MATH], we prove a cohomological vanishing result implying that any action on a CAT(0) cube complex fixes a vertex whenever every hyperplane stabilizer is solvable. As an application, we prove regularizability for actions of all higher-rank lattices by birational transformations on projective surfaces. We first use superrigidity for actions on infinite-dimensional real hyperbolic spaces to reduce to the de Jonqui\`eres group, and then apply our fixed-point theorem to the Jonqui\`eres complex. Our proof bypasses the direct use of property FW.
tldr: This paper proves a cohomological vanishing result for higher-rank lattices and applies it to regularize birational actions on projective surfaces.
motivation: To understand rigidity properties of higher-rank lattices acting on CAT(0) cube complexes and birational transformations.
method: Uses superrigidity for actions on infinite-dimensional real hyperbolic spaces and a fixed-point theorem on the Jonquières complex.
result: Proves that any action on a CAT(0) cube complex with solvable hyperplane stabilizers fixes a vertex, and regularizes birational actions on projective surfaces.
conclusion: The work advances the study of higher-rank lattice actions in geometric group theory and birational geometry.

title: Absolute Winning Exceptional Sets For Intermittent Interval Maps
authors: Jason Duvall
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for a Manneville--Pomeau type interval map, the set of points whose orbit closures miss a prescribed countable set is absolute winning in the sense of McMullen. The proof has three parts. First we directly prove that the exceptional set for the distinguished endpoint of the induced first-return map is absolute winning. Then we use the finite-branch winning theorem of Hu--Li--Yu, together with the one-dimensional implication from [MATH]-strong winning to absolute winning, to obtain absolute winning for all countable induced targets. Finally, a quasisymmetric pullback argument transfers these induced results back to the original map.
tldr: This paper proves that for a Manneville-Pomeau type interval map, the set of points whose orbit closures miss a prescribed countable set is absolute winning.
motivation: To understand the size and structure of exceptional sets in dynamical systems, specifically for intermittent interval maps.
method: The proof uses a three-part approach: first proving absolute winning for the distinguished endpoint of the induced first-return map, then applying the finite-branch winning theorem and the implication from strong winning to absolute winning, and finally using a quasisymmetric pullback argument.
result: The exceptional set for any countable target set is absolute winning, meaning it is a large set in the sense of Hausdorff dimension and game theory.
conclusion: The result establishes a strong winning property for exceptional sets in intermittent interval maps, contributing to the theory of dynamical systems and Diophantine approximation.

title: Off-site Enforcement Of Natural Conditions On Smooth Boundaries For Finite Elements Upon Fitted Straight-edged Triangular Meshes
authors: Vitoriano Ruas
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07963v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A few decades ago some possible remedies to an inaccurate enforcement of Neumann or Robin conditions prescribed on the boundary of a smooth domain, owing to the approximation of a curved domain by the union of straight-edged triangles or tetrahedra in a fitted mesh, were addressed in the literature. By that time authors such as Barrett and Elliott (1988) advocated the use of elements with a single curved edge or face fitting the true boundary not only at two or three vertexes, but also at additional points on those curves or curved surfaces, so as to define a polynomial surface of a certain type compatible with the theoretical approximation order of the method in use. In this work we adopt a different approach, whose main feature is the use of a fitted mesh consisting of straight-edged elements only. The recovery of lost accuracy due to the domain's approximation by a polytope is achieved by means of the addition of terms to the bilinear form, which account for natural boundary conditions of the same type to be prescribed on the approximating boundary, though much closer to the true ones. This technique is applied here to the case of triangular Lagrange finite elements, for which we give a rigorous reliability study in the solution of reaction-diffusion equations. Numerical experimentation is supplied in support of the theoretical results.
tldr: This paper presents a finite element method for enforcing Neumann or Robin boundary conditions on smooth domains using straight-edged triangular meshes with additional bilinear form terms.
motivation: Accurate enforcement of natural boundary conditions on curved domains is challenging when using straight-edged elements, leading to reduced accuracy.
method: The authors add correction terms to the bilinear form to account for the boundary approximation, applied to triangular Lagrange finite elements for reaction-diffusion equations.
result: Rigorous reliability analysis and numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence rates.
conclusion: The proposed technique recovers lost accuracy without using curved elements, offering a practical alternative for finite element simulations on fitted straight-edged meshes.

title: Polish Spaces Of Separable Banach Lattices
authors: Mariusz Niwi\'nski
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the descriptive complexity of classes of separable Banach lattices. Building on the theory of coding spaces for separable Banach spaces, we introduce two Polish space encodings of separable Banach lattices: one via closed sublattices of the universal lattice [MATH], and one via closed order ideals of the free Banach lattice [MATH]. We prove that, for every separable Banach lattice [MATH], the spaces of closed sublattices and of closed order ideals of [MATH] are Polish subspaces of the hyperspace of closed subsets of [MATH]. We also prove that the Fremlin projective tensor-product operation on ideal codes is [MATH]-measurable and has a [MATH] graph.
tldr: This paper studies the descriptive complexity of separable Banach lattices using Polish space encodings.
motivation: To understand the topological complexity of classes of Banach lattices, building on descriptive set theory for Banach spaces.
method: Introduces two Polish space encodings of separable Banach lattices via closed sublattices and closed order ideals, and analyzes measurability of the Fremlin projective tensor product.
result: Proves that spaces of closed sublattices and order ideals are Polish subspaces, and that the tensor product operation is Borel measurable.
conclusion: Provides a descriptive set-theoretic framework for studying separable Banach lattices.

title: A Non-Decoupled Time-Domain Direct Sampling Method For Inverse Elastic Medium Scattering
authors: Lefu Cai, Hongjie Li, Xianchao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work is concerned with an inverse medium problem for elastic waves, in which unknown inhomogeneities are reconstructed from time-resolved boundary measurements. We propose a novel time-domain direct sampling method for locating scatterers from a single incident source, without imposing specific assumptions on the temporal profile of the excitation. In particular, the imaging functional introduces a time-shifted correlation strategy that replaces the traditional [MATH]-[MATH] wave decomposition with a travel-time alignment mechanism, thereby enabling direct imaging from the coupled elastic wave field. To analyze the proposed time-domain imaging functional, we employ Parseval's identity for the Fourier--Laplace transform and reformulate the functional in the frequency domain. By exploiting properties of modified Bessel functions, we characterize the asymptotic behavior of the imaging functional and show that it attains its maximum at the target location, which enables reliable identification of the scatterer. Rigorous theoretical justifications are provided to substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Numerical experiments are also presented to demonstrate its performance and applicability.
tldr: This paper proposes a time-domain direct sampling method for inverse elastic medium scattering, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to locate unknown inhomogeneities in elastic media from time-resolved boundary measurements, a problem in classical inverse scattering theory.
method: A time-shifted correlation strategy is introduced to replace traditional wave decomposition, enabling direct imaging from coupled elastic wave fields. The imaging functional is analyzed using Fourier-Laplace transforms and modified Bessel functions.
result: The imaging functional attains its maximum at the target location, enabling reliable scatterer identification. Numerical experiments demonstrate performance.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a rigorous and effective approach for inverse elastic medium scattering, but it is entirely outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: Multi-type Sensor Placement For PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems
authors: Steven Maio, Alen Alexanderian, Karina Koval, Ruanui Nicholson
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address optimal placement of multi-type sensors for Bayesian inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). The proposed framework allows for sensors with different accuracies and observation types. We formulate the optimal experimental design (OED) problem as a knapsack-constrained binary optimization problem for maximizing expected information gain (EIG). To approximately solve the resulting optimization problems, we propose a stochastic cost-benefit greedy algorithm, which admits theoretical guarantees for monotone submodular set functions. Specifically, these guarantees apply in the case of linear Gaussian inverse problems with uncorrelated measurement errors, where the EIG admits a convenient closed-form expression. For nonlinear inverse problems, we develop a non-intrusive approach that uses the Bayesian approximation error framework to define an observation model with an error-corrected global linear model. We show that the corresponding approximate EIG is a lower bound for the exact EIG and thus provides a principled surrogate objective for the OED problem. The effectiveness of the proposed methods is demonstrated in two model inverse problems governed by PDEs.
tldr: This paper addresses optimal placement of multi-type sensors for Bayesian inverse problems governed by PDEs, focusing on maximizing expected information gain.
motivation: Efficient sensor placement is crucial for accurate inference in PDE-based inverse problems, but existing methods often assume single-type sensors or ignore cost constraints.
method: The authors formulate a knapsack-constrained binary optimization problem and propose a stochastic cost-benefit greedy algorithm with theoretical guarantees for monotone submodular set functions; for nonlinear problems, they use a Bayesian approximation error framework.
result: The greedy algorithm provides near-optimal solutions for linear Gaussian problems, and the approximate EIG for nonlinear problems is a lower bound for the exact EIG.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively handles multi-type sensors with different accuracies and costs, demonstrated on two model inverse problems.

title: Complex Dynamics Perspective For Birational Maps Of The Plane Arising From Cluster Algebra Mutations
authors: Andrei Grigorev, Krishna Chaitanya Kalidindi, Andres Quintero Santander, Roland Roeder
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the methods of holomorphic dynamics we investigate planar birational mappings that arise from the theory of cluster algebras and integrable systems. Computing dynamical degrees of these mappings, many of which are greater than one, allows us to show that many of the mappings do not have a conserved quantity (nor an invariant fibration). In most of the examples, invariant fibrations can also be ruled out by finding superattracting periodic points. This answers a question posted by Machacek and Ovenhouse 2024 and by Chen and Li 2024. Moreover, having found a good algebraically stable model for the mappings and having computed the dynamical degree, we can then apply results from the ergodic theory of birational maps to produce invariant measures with positive entropy and positive Lyapunov exponents.
tldr: This paper studies birational maps from cluster algebras using holomorphic dynamics, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to determine whether certain birational maps arising from cluster algebras have conserved quantities or invariant fibrations.
method: They compute dynamical degrees and find superattracting periodic points to rule out invariant fibrations, and apply ergodic theory to produce invariant measures.
result: Many of the maps have dynamical degree greater than one, indicating chaotic behavior and no conserved quantity.
conclusion: The paper answers open questions about the integrability of these maps and provides a dynamical systems perspective.

title: Generalization Theory For Through-the-Wall Radar Human Activity Recognition
authors: Weicheng Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Through-the-wall radar (TWR) human activity recognition (HAR) is important for non-line-of-sight indoor sensing, security monitoring, and emergency rescue. However, structured distribution shifts caused by person variation, observation-view variation, and wall-condition variation severely degrade recognition generalization, while the origin of the target-domain error still lacks a rigorous theoretical explanation. To address this issue, a generalization-analysis framework for TWR HAR is proposed in this paper. First, models for indoor human kinematics, TWR echo generation, radar image formation, feature representation, and bounded-weight neural networks are established within a unified source-to-target learning formulation. Then, the source risk, target risk, empirical risk, and admissible physical domain descriptor are defined, and a unified target-domain generalization bound is derived. Next, the structured shift term is decomposed into cross-person, cross-view, and cross-wall components, and the bound-tightening effects of physical low-dimensional representations, multi-source training, and parameter-space coverage are analyzed. Simulated and measured experiments jointly support the resulting theoretical analysis and illustrate its application value.
tldr: This paper proposes a generalization-analysis framework for through-the-wall radar human activity recognition, focusing on structured distribution shifts.
motivation: Structured distribution shifts caused by person, view, and wall variations degrade recognition generalization, and the origin of target-domain error lacks rigorous theoretical explanation.
method: Models for indoor human kinematics, TWR echo generation, radar image formation, feature representation, and bounded-weight neural networks are established within a unified source-to-target learning formulation, and a unified target-domain generalization bound is derived.
result: The structured shift term is decomposed into cross-person, cross-view, and cross-wall components, and bound-tightening effects of physical low-dimensional representations, multi-source training, and parameter-space coverage are analyzed.
conclusion: Simulated and measured experiments support the theoretical analysis and illustrate its application value.

title: Group Reduction, Formulas Solutions And Asymptotic Behavior Of A Class Of Fourth Order Difference Equations
authors: Tshifhiwa Murovhi, Mensah Folly-Gbetoula, Anani Kwassi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The symmetry method is a powerful and systematic approach for solving difference equations. It leverages the concept of transformations that leave a difference equation invariant, simplifying its structure and often reducing the equation to a solvable form. In this paper, the symmetry method is employed to study some class of difference equations. Using analytical techniques and computational tools, we derive explicit solutions for these equations and establish conditions for the existence of periodic solutions. Stability analysis is performed to identify non-hyperbolic points. Furthermore, some asymptotic properties of the difference equations are explored, with results and graphs illustrating how initial conditions and parameter values influence the behavior of the solutions.
tldr: This paper uses symmetry methods to solve a class of fourth-order difference equations, deriving explicit solutions and analyzing stability and asymptotic behavior.
motivation: To develop systematic methods for solving difference equations and understanding their solution behavior.
method: Applies Lie symmetry analysis to reduce the order of the difference equations and obtain exact solutions; uses analytical and computational tools.
result: Explicit solutions are derived, conditions for periodic solutions are established, and stability analysis identifies non-hyperbolic points.
conclusion: The symmetry method is effective for solving this class of difference equations, and the solutions exhibit diverse asymptotic behaviors depending on parameters.

title: Parameter Inference For Partially Observed Branching Processes
authors: Simone Baldassarri, Michel Mandjes, Jiesen Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study an age-dependent branching process. In the simplest setting, the population is divided into two age groups, namely juveniles and adults. Our objective is to estimate the model parameters using observations of the total population size only (i.e., juveniles plus adults). Focusing on the ergodic regime of the model, we introduce a method-of-moments estimator and establish its asymptotic normality. Several extensions are discussed, including models with more than two age groups.
tldr: This paper studies parameter estimation for age-dependent branching processes using only total population size observations.
motivation: Branching processes are used in population dynamics, epidemiology, and other fields; estimating parameters from partial observations is practically important.
method: A method-of-moments estimator is introduced for an age-dependent branching process with two age groups, and asymptotic normality is established.
result: The estimator is shown to be asymptotically normal in the ergodic regime; extensions to more age groups are discussed.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a way to infer model parameters from limited data, with potential applications in various scientific domains.

title: Algorithm Xxxx: Computation Of Finite Element Degree-of-freedom Transformation Matrices
authors: Garth N. Wells Matthew W. Scroggs
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08172v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The arithmetic intensity of algorithms for computing finite element operators increases with increasing polynomial degree. This has made high degree methods particularly attractive on modern CPU and GPU architectures, since on these architectures performance at low degree is limited (severely) by the available memory bandwidth and only a very small fraction of the floating point capacity of the processor is used. Higher degree methods can exploit a significantly greater fraction of the available compute power of modern architectures. However, whilst stable methods for computing high-degree finite element bases are well-established, there is no universal and automated algorithm for the efficient construction of the degree-of-freedom map for arbitrary degree elements. We address this with a new algorithm that can be used in computing degree-of-freedom maps for an arbitrary Ciarlet-type finite element using only the element's definition and properties of the reference cell, and without requiring a specific implementation for each element. This method is implemented in the library Basix, a component of the FEniCSx libraries. As well as allowing vast simplifications of parts of a codebase, the algorithm allows for new elements to be implemented with ease and has allowed us to support user-defined custom elements that a user can create at runtime without requiring the user to input any information about transformations required to construct a degree-of-freedom map.
tldr: This paper presents an algorithm for computing degree-of-freedom transformation matrices for arbitrary Ciarlet-type finite elements, enabling efficient implementation of high-degree finite element methods.
motivation: High-degree finite element methods are attractive for modern architectures but lack a universal algorithm for constructing degree-of-freedom maps, which is essential for efficient computation.
method: The algorithm uses only the element's definition and properties of the reference cell to compute the transformation matrices, without requiring element-specific implementations.
result: The algorithm is implemented in the Basix library (part of FEniCSx), simplifying codebases and enabling user-defined custom elements at runtime.
conclusion: This work provides a general and automated solution for degree-of-freedom map construction, facilitating the use of high-degree finite elements in scientific computing.

title: Accelerated Golden Ratio Primal--Dual Algorithm For Structured Convex Optimisation Without Linesearch
authors: V. Vetrivel Santanu Soe
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper revisits the adaptive extended golden-ratio primal--dual algorithm (aEGRPDA) proposed by Soe et al. (2026) for structured convex optimisation problems involving a differentiable term that is only locally smooth. We prove that the artificial upper bound imposed on the primal step-size in aEGRPDA is redundant, since the adaptive rule itself keeps the step-sizes bounded above. As a consequence, the ergodic [MATH] estimates for the objective residual and feasibility violation, where [MATH] denotes the number of iterations, are independent of this hyperparameter. Consequently, the resulting adaptive golden-ratio primal--dual method, therefore, requires neither a step-size cap, nor a linesearch procedure, nor a known global Lipschitz constant. We establish linear convergence of the algorithm when both the primal and dual functions are strongly convex. Furthermore, we develop two accelerated variants, in addition to the local smoothness assumption: one for the case where the nonsmooth primal component is strongly convex, and another for the case where the differentiable term is globally strongly convex. For these accelerated methods, we prove an ergodic [MATH] convergence rate. Preliminary numerical experiments on a Poisson imaging problem illustrate the efficiency and robustness of the proposed approaches.
tldr: This paper presents an accelerated primal-dual algorithm for structured convex optimization without linesearch, focusing on convergence rates and numerical experiments on Poisson imaging.
motivation: The authors aim to remove the need for a step-size cap, linesearch, or global Lipschitz constant in the adaptive extended golden-ratio primal-dual algorithm, making it more practical.
method: They prove that the adaptive rule inherently bounds primal step-sizes, eliminating the artificial upper bound, and develop two accelerated variants under strong convexity assumptions.
result: The algorithm achieves ergodic O(1/N^2) convergence rates for objective residual and feasibility violation, and linear convergence when both primal and dual functions are strongly convex.
conclusion: The proposed method is efficient and robust, as demonstrated on a Poisson imaging problem, and requires no hyperparameter tuning beyond the adaptive rule.

title: On The Stability Of Proximal Operators In Wasserstein Spaces Under Different Notions Of Convexity
authors: Simone Di Marino, Sara Farinelli, Emanuele Naldi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The proximal operator is a fundamental tool in variational analysis and optimization. In the setting of a Hilbert space, given a proper, lower semicontinuous convex functional, its proximal operator is non-expansive, that is, 1-Lipschitz continuous. In the Wasserstein setting, the contraction properties of this operator have been investigated from different perspectives by Carlen and Craig and Adve and M\'esz\'aros, among others, and are not completely understood. In this paper, we study the stability properties of proximal maps, with a particular focus on non-expansivity, under various notions of convexity of the functional that can be considered in the Wasserstein space.
tldr: This paper studies the stability (non-expansivity) of proximal operators in Wasserstein spaces under different convexity notions.
motivation: The contraction properties of proximal operators in Wasserstein spaces are not fully understood, and this work aims to clarify stability under various convexity definitions.
method: The authors analyze proximal maps in the Wasserstein space, considering different notions of convexity (e.g., geodesic convexity, lambda-convexity) and derive conditions for non-expansivity.
result: They provide conditions under which proximal operators are non-expansive (1-Lipschitz) in the Wasserstein metric, extending known results from Hilbert spaces.
conclusion: The stability of proximal operators in Wasserstein spaces depends critically on the type of convexity assumed, with some notions preserving non-expansivity and others not.

title: Sub-Infinite Horizon Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control Problems And Delayed Backward Riccati Equations
authors: Yutao Chen, Hongwei Lou, Hanxiao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate a class of so-called sub-infinite horizon stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problems, in which the initial time [MATH] is arbitrarily taken from [MATH] and the running cost is defined over [MATH] for a given [MATH]. The optimal control of this type of problem can be obtained by standard methods; however, it is shown that the resulting optimal control is generally time-inconsistent. Thus, instead of seeking an optimal control, which is time-inconsistent, we aim to find a time-consistent, locally optimal, and time-invariant equilibrium strategy, by introducing a new and very interesting type of Riccati equation. Its main feature is that the generator depends on a delay term of the unknown. In other words, this Riccati equation is a backward ordinary differential equation (ODE) with delay, which is equivalent to a forward ODE with advanced terms. Such an equation is essentially a Fredholm integral equation, whose solvability is challenging. We overcome the difficulty by deriving a sharp a priori estimate and applying the Leray--Schauder fixed point theorem. To this end, we establish a comparison theorem between two matrix-valued nonlinear algebraic equations. The convergence behavior of the solution to the Riccati equation as [MATH] is also provided.
tldr: This paper studies sub-infinite horizon stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problems and introduces a delayed backward Riccati equation to find time-consistent equilibrium strategies.
motivation: Standard optimal control for this class of problems yields time-inconsistent solutions, so the authors seek a time-consistent, locally optimal, and time-invariant equilibrium strategy.
method: They formulate a new type of Riccati equation with delay, which is a backward ODE with delay equivalent to a forward ODE with advanced terms, and solve it using a priori estimates and the Leray-Schauder fixed point theorem.
result: They establish solvability of the delayed Riccati equation and analyze convergence behavior as the horizon parameter tends to infinity.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for obtaining time-consistent strategies in sub-infinite horizon stochastic control problems, but it is purely in classical control theory with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: 3d Virtual Element Method For Advection-Diffusion-Reaction Problems With Variable Coefficients On Locally Quasi-Uniform Polytopes
authors: M. Trezzi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze a Continuous Interior Penalty (CIP) stabilized Virtual Element Method (VEM) for three-dimensional advection-diffusion-reaction equations on general polyhedral meshes. While CIP-VEM schemes have been recently explored in a two-dimensional setting, their analysis heavily relies on global mesh quasi-uniformity and constant physical parameters. We overcome these limitations by introducing a novel three-dimensional variant of the Oswald-type quasi-interpolant. This allows us to establish robust, uniform error estimates in the hyperbolic limit under a realistic local quasi-uniformity assumption and variable coefficients. Finally, we provide a comprehensive set of three-dimensional numerical experiments to validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the absence of non-physical oscillations.
tldr: This paper presents a stabilized virtual element method for 3D advection-diffusion-reaction problems on polyhedral meshes.
motivation: Existing CIP-VEM schemes are limited to 2D and require global mesh quasi-uniformity and constant coefficients; this work extends to 3D with variable coefficients under local quasi-uniformity.
method: A novel 3D Oswald-type quasi-interpolant is introduced to enable robust error estimates, and the method is analyzed using continuous interior penalty stabilization.
result: Uniform error estimates are proven in the hyperbolic limit, and numerical experiments confirm theoretical convergence rates without non-physical oscillations.
conclusion: The proposed 3D CIP-VEM is effective for advection-diffusion-reaction problems on general polyhedral meshes with variable coefficients.

title: On Absolute Strong Exposure For Lipschitz Maps
authors: Mingu Jung Geunsu Choi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce strongly exposing Lipschitz maps, a vector-valued extension of Weaver's peaking functions and a nonlinear analogue of absolutely strongly exposing operators. Our main result shows that a Lipschitz map is strongly exposing if and only if its canonical linearization is absolutely strongly exposing. This equivalence serves as a bridge between the linear and Lipschitz settings and enables us to transfer several results from the former to the latter. As applications, we establish norm-denseness and residuality results for strongly exposing Lipschitz maps, obtain an isomorphic characterization related to the denseness of strongly norm-attaining Lipschitz maps. We also investigate weak sequential denseness of strongly exposing Lipschitz maps. In particular, we prove that this property holds whenever the derived set of the underlying metric space is finite, while further examples show that, unlike for strongly norm-attaining Lipschitz maps, weak sequential denseness may fail beyond trivial cases.
tldr: This paper introduces strongly exposing Lipschitz maps and establishes an equivalence with absolutely strongly exposing operators, with applications to denseness and residuality results.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the concept of strongly exposing operators to the nonlinear setting of Lipschitz maps, bridging linear and Lipschitz analysis.
method: They define strongly exposing Lipschitz maps and prove that a Lipschitz map is strongly exposing iff its canonical linearization is absolutely strongly exposing, using functional analysis and Banach space theory.
result: They obtain norm-denseness and residuality results for strongly exposing Lipschitz maps, an isomorphic characterization, and weak sequential denseness under certain conditions.
conclusion: The work establishes a bridge between linear and Lipschitz settings, transferring results and revealing limitations of weak sequential denseness.

title: Splitting Methods For Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equation Without Order Reduction
authors: Bego\~na Cano Carlos Arranz-Sim\'on
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A technique is provided in this paper to integrate nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with time-dependent Dirichlet boundary conditions with high-order Yoshida splittings which are based on Strang method. For that, a modification of Strang method is required in which the linear and stiff part of the equation is integrated with a rational-like version of midpoint rule for which the required boundary values can be calculated without resorting to any differentiation of data. Although Yoshida splitting (with real coefficients) cannot be applied to parabolic problems to obtain order higher than two because of stability, the modified Strang method is also applicable to such type of problems and local order [MATH] and global order [MATH] are also obtained without differentiation of data.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for integrating the nonlinear Schrödinger equation with time-dependent boundary conditions using high-order Yoshida splittings.
motivation: Standard splitting methods suffer from order reduction when applied to problems with time-dependent boundary conditions; the authors aim to overcome this limitation.
method: A modified Strang method is introduced, where the linear stiff part is integrated using a rational-like midpoint rule that avoids differentiation of boundary data, enabling high-order Yoshida splittings.
result: The modified method achieves local and global order without order reduction, and is also applicable to parabolic problems.
conclusion: The proposed technique allows high-order integration of nonlinear Schrödinger and parabolic equations with time-dependent boundary conditions without order reduction.

title: Hankel's Principle As An anti-Kantian Program
authors: Iulian D. Toader
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hankel used his principle of the permanence of formal laws (PFL) as a guide for the extension of number systems and as a necessary condition for the legitimacy of their formal theories. He acknowledged that these applications have important limitations, evidenced by the extension to hypercomplex numbers and by what he saw as the unavoidable inconsistency of a formal theory of irrational numbers. Yet, intriguingly enough, he remained fully committed to the PFL. I argue that this was due to his understanding it as an expression of a conservative strategy, inherited from Peacock and Hamilton, which permits the revision of the basic laws of arithmetic if there are reasons for revision that are found, upon deliberation, to outweigh the reasons for their preservation. Then I discuss criticisms by Schubert and Pringsheim, who reformulated the PFL to align it with their own anti-revisionary conservative strategy, at the cost of relinquishing parts of modern mathematics. I conclude by emphasizing the deep philosophical difference between these kinds of conservatism in mathematics.
tldr: This paper discusses Hankel's principle of the permanence of formal laws as a conservative strategy in the philosophy of mathematics, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The author aims to clarify Hankel's commitment to the PFL despite its limitations, and to contrast it with other conservative strategies in mathematics.
method: Historical and philosophical analysis of Hankel's writings and subsequent criticisms by Schubert and Pringsheim.
result: Hankel's PFL is interpreted as a revisionary conservative strategy, while Schubert and Pringsheim's reformulations are anti-revisionary.
conclusion: The paper highlights deep philosophical differences between kinds of conservatism in mathematics.

title: An Exact Distribution-Free Test For Means Of Nonnegative Random Variables
authors: Philip S. Thomas Nikos Vlassis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] be independent nonnegative random variables, not necessarily identically distributed. Let [MATH] be independent of [MATH], and define [MATH]. We prove that, for every [MATH], whenever [MATH] for every [MATH], [MATH] for all [MATH]. Thus [MATH] is a finite-sample, distribution-free [MATH]-value for testing the null hypothesis [MATH] for all [MATH]. This proves a conjecture of Gaffke (2005).
tldr: This paper proves a distribution-free test for means of nonnegative random variables, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses a problem in classical statistics, specifically testing the mean of nonnegative random variables without distributional assumptions.
method: The authors prove a finite-sample, distribution-free p-value for the null hypothesis that the mean of each random variable is less than or equal to a given threshold, using a martingale argument.
result: They show that for any threshold, the probability of falsely rejecting the null is bounded by the threshold, providing a valid test.
conclusion: The result confirms a conjecture by Gaffke (2005) and offers a practical tool for nonparametric hypothesis testing.

title: High-order Complete Flux Schemes For Convection-diffusion Equations On Arbitrary Subdivisions
authors: Peng Yang, Wenyu Lei, Liwei Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a complete flux finite volume method for convection-diffusion equations that works on arbitrary meshes in two and three dimensions and for discrete spaces of any polynomial degree. Unlike standard finite volume discretizations, where the numerical flux is directly approximated from the flux definition, we derive the exact normal flux across each control volume edge/face from the underlying PDE. This exact flux splits naturally into a homogeneous part (the classical Scharfetter-Gummel flux) and an inhomogeneous part expressed via a Green's function that incorporates the tangential flux and the source term. The resulting formulation is exactly equivalent to the continuous equation and, once the discrete space is chosen, yields high-order schemes without any correction or stabilization. For piecewise linear spaces, the scheme achieves optimal second-order accuracy in convection-dominated regimes and can preserve positivity on moderately coarse meshes. For quadratic spaces, standard finite volume methods, based on the Lagrange elements or B-splines, fail to attain optimal [MATH] convergence unless the control volume mesh is specially designed. The proposed complete flux scheme, however, always achieves optimal [MATH] convergence independently of the control volume mesh. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm the robustness and optimal accuracy of the approach.
tldr: This paper presents a high-order complete flux finite volume method for convection-diffusion equations on arbitrary meshes.
motivation: Standard finite volume methods often require special meshes or corrections to achieve high-order accuracy, especially for convection-dominated problems.
method: The authors derive an exact normal flux expression from the PDE, splitting it into homogeneous and inhomogeneous parts, and discretize using arbitrary polynomial spaces.
result: The scheme achieves optimal second-order accuracy for linear spaces and optimal convergence for quadratic spaces regardless of mesh, unlike standard methods.
conclusion: The proposed complete flux scheme is robust and achieves optimal accuracy on arbitrary meshes for convection-diffusion equations.

title: An Iterative Method For Transient Finite Element Simulations Of Non-Linear Eddy Current Problems
authors: Haik Silm Karl Hollaus
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A method is presented to carry out a transient simulation of eddy current problems with nonlinear materials. Coils are voltage-driven. The magnetic field due to currents in coils are considered by their Biot-Savart-fields. The magnetic vector potential is used in the finite element formulation. The time stepping method is based on implicit Euler. The arising nonlinear equation system is split into two parts, the common finite element system and a circuit equation. Each part is solved separately by Newton's method. Additionally, a line search is used to solve the nonlinear field equations. Inrush currents and average magnetic flux densities through cross sections of laminates of a nonlinear benchmark problem consisting of a laminated iron core inserted in a cylindrical coil are studied. All details of the numerical benchmark are given to evaluate the presented results. Numerical data describing the performance of the presented method are provided.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for transient finite element simulations of nonlinear eddy current problems.
motivation: To efficiently simulate eddy currents in nonlinear magnetic materials for engineering applications.
method: Splits the nonlinear system into finite element and circuit equations, solved separately with Newton's method and line search.
result: Demonstrates the method on a benchmark problem with laminated iron core, showing inrush currents and flux densities.
conclusion: The proposed iterative method effectively handles nonlinear eddy current problems with voltage-driven coils.

title: Construction And Upper Bound On The Minimum Genus Of An Embedded Surface With Anosov Geodesic Flow
authors: Daniel Visscher Victor Donnay
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We create examples of smooth, compact surfaces in [MATH] for which the geodesic flow is Anosov. We determine their genus, thereby giving a (non-sharp) upper bound for the minimal genus of an embedded surface with Anosov geodesic flow. These examples are explicit physically realizable Anosov systems.
tldr: This paper constructs smooth compact surfaces with Anosov geodesic flow and provides an upper bound on the minimal genus of such surfaces.
motivation: To find explicit examples of physically realizable Anosov systems and determine the minimal genus of embedded surfaces that support Anosov geodesic flow.
method: The authors construct explicit examples of surfaces embedded in R^3 with Anosov geodesic flow and compute their genus to derive an upper bound.
result: They provide a non-sharp upper bound for the minimal genus of an embedded surface with Anosov geodesic flow.
conclusion: The examples demonstrate that such surfaces exist and the genus bound can be improved in future work.

title: A Screening Approach To Nonparametric Inference From The M/g/1 Workload
authors: Binyamin Kobzantsev Royi Jacobovic
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address a long-standing open problem posed by Hansen and Pitts (2006) on nonparametric inference for the service-time distribution in an M/G/1 workload model. We consider an M/G/1 queue with unknown arrival rate [MATH] and service-time distribution [MATH], without assuming stability or stationarity. A statistician observes the workload process at discrete times [MATH] and aims to estimate [MATH] at a fixed point [MATH]. We propose an estimator [MATH] based solely on the observed workload trajectory. The construction relies on a screening mechanism that extracts conditionally i.i.d. compound Poisson increments from the workload process, thereby reducing the dependent-data problem to a Laplace-transform inversion framework. Under mild regularity assumptions on [MATH], i.e., continuous differentiability on [MATH], twice differentiability at [MATH], and a finite second moment, we establish the bound \[ \bigl|B_n(w)-B(w)\bigr| =\!\left({}\right), \qquad n\to\infty. \]This provides the first solution to the Hansen-Pitts problem achieving a parametric [MATH]-risk rate (up to a logarithmic factor), without requiring stationarity, stability, or knowledge of the arrival rate.
tldr: This paper solves a nonparametric inference problem for the M/G/1 queue workload process using a screening approach to extract i.i.d. increments.
motivation: The authors address a long-standing open problem on nonparametric estimation of the service-time distribution in an M/G/1 queue without assuming stability or stationarity.
method: They propose an estimator based on a screening mechanism that extracts conditionally i.i.d. compound Poisson increments from the workload process, reducing the dependent-data problem to Laplace-transform inversion.
result: Under mild regularity assumptions, they establish a parametric rate (up to a logarithmic factor) for the estimator's risk, providing the first solution to the Hansen-Pitts problem.
conclusion: The work offers a novel statistical method for queueing systems, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Second Order Systems On Hilbert Spaces With Nonlinear Damping
authors: George Weiss Shantanu Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.08506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a special class of nonlinear infinite dimensional systems. These systems are obtained by modifying the second order differential equation that is part of the description of conservative linear systems out of thin air introduced by M. Tucsnak and G. Weiss in 2003. The modified differential equation contains a new nonlinear damping term, that is maximal monotone and possibly set-valued. We show that this new class of nonlinear infinite dimensional systems is incrementally scattering passive (hence well-posed). Our approach uses the theory of maximal monotone operators and the Crandall-Pazy theorem about nonlinear contraction semigroups, which we apply to a Lax-Phillips type nonlinear semigroup that represents the whole system. We illustrate our result on the n-dimensional wave equation.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with nonlinear damping, focusing on well-posedness and passivity, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to extend the theory of conservative linear systems to include nonlinear damping, motivated by applications in control theory and partial differential equations.
method: They modify a second-order differential equation from conservative linear systems by adding a maximal monotone nonlinear damping term, and use maximal monotone operator theory and the Crandall-Pazy theorem to analyze the resulting nonlinear semigroup.
result: They prove that the new class of systems is incrementally scattering passive and well-posed, and illustrate the result on the n-dimensional wave equation.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with damping, but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Carnap Ten Years Later: Lessons Learned And Next Steps
authors: Graham Leach-Krouse
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The first part of this paper provides an experience report, recounting the design and long-term maintenance of the Carnap proof assistant framework used cumulatively by over 45,000 students worldwide over the last decade. We cover the good, the bad, and the ugly: what worked well, what didn't work, and what added friction to development and maintenance over time. These insights motivate a bottom-up redesign of the Carnap framework, which is the topic of the paper's second part. Briefly, the new design combines a new high-performance verifier kernel (mm0-zig) targeting Mario Carneiro's metamath zero format, and the Aufbau Bytecode Compiler, (abc), a new proof compiler that can serve as a backend for richly interactive proof-authoring experiences on the web.
tldr: This paper reports on the design and maintenance of the Carnap proof assistant framework and proposes a bottom-up redesign using mm0-zig and the Aufbau Bytecode Compiler.
motivation: To share lessons learned from a decade of developing and maintaining the Carnap proof assistant, and to motivate a new architecture for improved performance and maintainability.
method: The authors provide an experience report based on the Carnap framework's history, then describe a new design combining a high-performance verifier kernel (mm0-zig) and a proof compiler (abc) for web-based interactive proof authoring.
result: The paper presents insights into what worked and what didn't in Carnap, and outlines a new architecture that aims to address these issues.
conclusion: The new design promises better performance and a richer interactive experience, but the paper is a proposal and experience report rather than a completed implementation or evaluation.

title: Controllability-Aware Adversarial Examples Against LLM-Based Network Traffic Classifiers
authors: Zhenpeng Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored as network intrusion detection classifiers, but their adversarial robustness under realistic attacker constraints remains unclear. We present a controllability-aware black-box transfer framework for LLM-based network traffic classifiers. The framework partitions flow features into directly controllable (DC), indirectly controllable (IC), and uncontrollable (UC) groups according to network communication semantics, then restricts perturbations to DC features while freezing IC/UC features. Using a shared XGBoost surrogate, we generate finite-difference PGD, greedy coordinate-wise, and NES adversarial examples and transfer them to seven LLM targets and two conventional ML targets across five IDS benchmarks from 1999 to 2022. Across 27 valid LLM configurations and over 500,000 adversarial examples, we find that LLM transfer vulnerability is substantial but dataset- and comparator-dependent. Compared with LightGBM, LLMs are more vulnerable on RT-IoT2022 and CIC-IDS-2018, comparable on NSL-KDD and UNSW-NB15, and less vulnerable on HIKARI-2021; compared with the averaged ML baseline, LLMs show higher ASR on all five datasets. We further observe a consistent cross-architecture transfer hierarchy: gradient- and score-based perturbations transfer more effectively than greedy perturbations across all 27 LLM cells and 9/10 ML cells. Cross-surrogate validation with tree, neural, and linear surrogates yields similar LLM ASR, reducing evidence that the findings are XGBoost-specific. Constraint violation rate is 0\% by construction.
tldr: This paper studies adversarial robustness of LLM-based network traffic classifiers under realistic controllability constraints.
motivation: LLMs are increasingly used for network intrusion detection, but their adversarial robustness under realistic attacker constraints is not well understood.
method: The authors propose a controllability-aware black-box transfer framework that partitions flow features into controllable and uncontrollable groups, and generates adversarial examples using finite-difference PGD, greedy coordinate-wise, and NES methods with an XGBoost surrogate.
result: LLMs show substantial transfer vulnerability that varies across datasets and comparators; gradient- and score-based perturbations transfer more effectively than greedy ones.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for robustness evaluation of LLM-based classifiers under realistic constraints, but the paper does not contribute to quantum information theory or related fields.

title: Forensic Schema For Psychological Manipulation In Cyber Fraud: LLM-Driven Victim Reports Analysis
authors: Zikai Alex Wen, Corrazon Ogot, Juan Li, Yan Bai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing cybercrime classification schemas capture contact metadata and financial transactions but omit the psychological manipulation techniques perpetrators employ. We present a forensic schema (four categories, 35 questions) adding 11 manipulation indicators and cryptocurrency evidence fields to established forensic foundations. Applied to 10,994 victim reports via large language model (LLM)-driven annotation and validated against two human annotators (mean LLM-human [MATH], matching inter-annotator [MATH]), the schema revealed a statistically distinct manipulation profile for each major fraud type (Cramer's [MATH] up to [MATH]). A rationale-based evidence audit nonetheless exposed a forensic detail gap: detection of manipulation techniques was reliable, but victim narratives varied widely in the actionable detail supporting each Yes answer, and blockchain-specific identifiers were nearly absent. These findings point to AI-assisted victim intake with schema-informed follow-up questions as the most direct way to close the gap. The tiered annotation strategy also provides a reusable template for LLM-based extraction from other forensic text domains.
tldr: This paper presents a forensic schema for analyzing psychological manipulation in cyber fraud using LLM-driven victim report analysis.
motivation: Existing cybercrime classification schemas omit psychological manipulation techniques, which are crucial for understanding and combating fraud.
method: The authors developed a forensic schema with 35 questions across four categories, including 11 manipulation indicators and cryptocurrency evidence fields, and applied it to 10,994 victim reports using LLM annotation validated against human annotators.
result: The schema revealed distinct manipulation profiles for different fraud types, but a forensic detail gap was identified: detection of manipulation was reliable, but victim narratives lacked actionable detail and blockchain identifiers were nearly absent.
conclusion: AI-assisted victim intake with schema-informed follow-up questions is the most direct way to close the forensic detail gap, and the tiered annotation strategy provides a reusable template for other forensic text domains.

title: ScopeJudge: Cost-Aware Pre-Execution Gating For Offensive Security Agents
authors: Shane Caldwell, Max Harley, Ads Dawson, Michael Kouremetis, Vincent Abruzzo, Will Pearce
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLM agents take on offensive security work, a single out-of-scope tool call can breach a client's engagement boundary, disrupt production, or void a bug-bounty finding. Unlike a fixed safety policy, the boundary that matters is declared in the user's request and must be inferred from intent. That challenge is sharpened by the adversarial nature of offensive security: the same tool call is in or out of scope depending not on the action itself but on the target it touches and the context in which it runs, which no fixed policy can enumerate in advance. We study pre-execution gating: a cheap, trusted LLM judge inspects each call proposed by a strong, swappable agent, and accepts or rejects it before it runs. We introduce ScopeJudge, a benchmark of 4,897 tool calls (7.7% scope violations) from agent trajectories on tasks engineered to tempt agents out of scope and labeled at the call level by professional penetration testers, with substantial inter-grader agreement (Fleiss kappa = 0.64) that sets an expert agreement reference point of F1 = 0.78. We evaluate eight judge models under five transcript strategies, varying how much context the judge sees, from the static policy alone to the full raw transcript, and chart the resulting cost-accuracy Pareto frontier. We find that a static policy is structurally insufficient for scope enforcement: blind to the user's request, judge recall collapses to near zero, confirming that scope lives in the request and that request-conditioned monitoring is necessary. Because a missed violation costs more than a spurious rejection, we report precision, recall, and F1 separately and recommend two operating points: a cost-sensitive configuration and a recall-first one for high-stakes deployments. We release the ScopeJudge dataset to support real-time monitoring and scalable oversight of autonomous security agents.
tldr: This paper introduces ScopeJudge, a benchmark and pre-execution gating method for LLM agents in offensive security to prevent out-of-scope tool calls.
motivation: Offensive security agents risk breaching client boundaries or causing harm if they execute out-of-scope actions; a static policy cannot capture scope defined by user intent.
method: A cheap LLM judge inspects each tool call proposed by a strong agent, using varying amounts of context (from static policy to full transcript), and accepts or rejects before execution.
result: Static policy alone fails (recall near zero); request-conditioned monitoring is necessary. The benchmark includes 4,897 labeled calls with expert agreement (Fleiss kappa=0.64).
conclusion: Pre-execution gating with request-aware judges is effective for scope enforcement, with recommended operating points for cost-sensitive or recall-first deployments.

title: Open Models, Open Risks: Measuring Unsafe Generation In Text-to-Image Models In The Wild
authors: Peilin Han, Yang Liu, Yilong Yang, Jingchun Zhang, Teng Li, Jianfeng Ma, Zhuo Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2607.07827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing safety studies on text-to-image (T2I) jailbreaks are largely conducted in controlled in-the-lab settings, typically on a small number of canonical models. As a result, the current safety status of the rapidly growing in-the-wild T2I ecosystem remains unclear. This uncertainty is amplified by two factors: existing detector-based metrics are designed for controlled evaluation, and in-the-wild risks may arise not only from adversarial prompting, but also from unsafe release practices and unsafe model derivatives. In this paper, we present a large-scale empirical study of in-the-wild T2I safety through the lens of jailbreak.
